1: //! The fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode.
2: //!
3: //! Layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`):
4: //!
5: //! ```text
6: //! [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
7: //! ```
8: //!
9: //! All multi-byte fields are little-endian on the wire. `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`,
10: //! so a 64-byte cache line holds exactly 4 opcodes.
11: 
12: use core::ptr;
13: 
14: /// Size of one opcode in bytes.
15: pub const OPCODE_SIZE: usize = 16;
16: 
17: /// A fixed-size 16-byte opcode.
18: ///
19: /// This struct intentionally mirrors the wire layout and is `#[repr(C, packed)]`
20: /// per the specification. Because it is packed, fields may be unaligned; always
21: /// read fields through the accessor methods (which use unaligned reads) rather
22: /// than by value.
23: #[repr(C, packed)]
24: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
25: pub struct Opcode {
26:     /// Opcode category (see `constants::Category`).
27:     pub category: u8,
28:     /// Command within the category (see `constants::Command*`).
29:     pub command: u8,
30:     /// Category/command-specific flags.
31:     pub flags: u16,
32:     /// Primary payload.
33:     pub a: u32,
34:     /// Secondary payload.
35:     pub b: u32,
36:     /// Tertiary payload.
37:     pub c: u32,
38: }
39: 
40: impl Opcode {
41:     /// Byte size of an opcode (`16`).
42:     pub const SIZE: usize = OPCODE_SIZE;
43: 
44:     /// Construct an opcode from raw fields.
45:     #[inline]
46:     pub const fn new(category: u8, command: u8, flags: u16, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) -> Self {
47:         Self {
48:             category,
49:             command,
50:             flags,
51:             a,
52:             b,
53:             c,
54:         }
55:     }
56: 
57:     /// The opcode category.
58:     #[inline]
59:     pub fn category(&self) -> u8 {
60:         self.category
61:     }
62: 
63:     /// The command within the category.
64:     #[inline]
65:     pub fn command(&self) -> u8 {
66:         self.command
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// The 16-bit flags word.
70:     #[inline]
71:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
72:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
73:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() }
74:     }
75: 
76:     /// Primary payload (little-endian u32).
77:     #[inline]
78:     pub fn a(&self) -> u32 {
79:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
80:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() }
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Secondary payload (little-endian u32).
84:     #[inline]
85:     pub fn b(&self) -> u32 {
86:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
87:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() }
88:     }
89: 
90:     /// Tertiary payload (little-endian u32).
91:     #[inline]
92:     pub fn c(&self) -> u32 {
93:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
94:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() }
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Interpret `A` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
98:     #[inline]
99:     pub fn a_f32(&self) -> f32 {
100:         f32::from_bits(self.a())
101:     }
102: 
103:     /// Interpret `B` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
104:     #[inline]
105:     pub fn b_f32(&self) -> f32 {
106:         f32::from_bits(self.b())
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Interpret `C` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
110:     #[inline]
111:     pub fn c_f32(&self) -> f32 {
112:         f32::from_bits(self.c())
113:     }
114: 
115:     /// Serialize to the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
116:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] {
117:         let mut out = [0u8; OPCODE_SIZE];
118:         out[0] = self.category;
119:         out[1] = self.command;
120:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
121:         let flags = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() };
122:         let a = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() };
123:         let b = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() };
124:         let c = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() };
125:         out[2..4].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
126:         out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&a.to_le_bytes());
127:         out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&b.to_le_bytes());
128:         out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&c.to_le_bytes());
129:         out
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Deserialize from the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
133:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8; OPCODE_SIZE]) -> Self {
134:         let category = bytes[0];
135:         let command = bytes[1];
136:         let flags = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[2], bytes[3]]);
137:         let a = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
138:         let b = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
139:         let c = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap());
140:         Self {
141:             category,
142:             command,
143:             flags,
144:             a,
145:             b,
146:             c,
147:         }
148:     }
149: }
150: 
151: #[cfg(test)]
152: mod tests {
153:     use super::*;
154: 
155:     #[test]
156:     fn size_is_16_bytes() {
157:         assert_eq!(core::mem::size_of::<Opcode>(), 16);
158:     }
159: 
160:     #[test]
161:     fn round_trips_through_bytes() {
162:         let op = Opcode::new(0x01, 0x01, 0x0001, 0x1122_3344, 0x5566_7788, 0x99AA_BBCC);
163:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();
164:         let back = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
165:         assert_eq!(op, back);
166:     }
167: 
168:     #[test]
169:     fn known_byte_layout() {
170:         // TREE / CREATE_NODE, no flags, nodeId=1, componentType=VSTACK(0x0010), c=0
171:         let op = Opcode::new(0x01, 0x01, 0x0000, 1, 0x0010, 0);
172:         assert_eq!(
173:             op.to_bytes(),
174:             [0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]
175:         );
176:     }
177: 
178:     #[test]
179:     fn float_payloads_round_trip() {
180:         let op = Opcode::new(0x02, 0x01, 0, 42, 100.0f32.to_bits(), 200.0f32.to_bits());
181:         let back = Opcode::from_bytes(&op.to_bytes());
182:         assert_eq!(back.a(), 42);
183:         assert_eq!(back.b_f32(), 100.0);
184:         assert_eq!(back.c_f32(), 200.0);
185:     }
186: }

(End of file - total 186 lines)
</content>

1: //! Protocol constants: categories, commands, component types, value types, flags.
2: //!
3: //! These constants are part of the wire protocol (see `spec/OPCODE.md`) and MUST
4: //! NOT be renumbered once released. Component types were renumbered pre-release
5: //! to the grouped ranges in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` (wire version stays 1).
6: 
7: /// Opcode categories (`Category` field, u8).
8: pub mod category {
9:     /// Tree mutations (guest → host): node create/delete/insert/remove/move.
10:     pub const TREE: u8 = 0x01;
11:     /// Parameters and design tokens (guest → host): the constraint properties
12:     /// (spacing, padding, alignment, …) and content that native renderers use
13:     /// to lay out and style native elements. The engine does NOT emit rects.
14:     pub const PARAMETER: u8 = 0x02;
15:     /// Raw input events (host → guest): pointer down/move/up, key down/up.
16:     pub const EVENT: u8 = 0x03;
17:     /// Control (both directions): reset, environment, custom data.
18:     pub const META: u8 = 0x04;
19: }
20: 
21: /// Commands within the `TREE` category.
22: pub mod tree {
23:     /// `A=nodeId, B=componentType (u16, low)`
24:     pub const CREATE_NODE: u8 = 0x01;
25:     /// `A=nodeId`
26:     pub const DELETE_NODE: u8 = 0x02;
27:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=index` (append is `C = u32::MAX`, see [`crate::APPEND`])
28:     pub const INSERT_CHILD: u8 = 0x03;
29:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId`
30:     pub const REMOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x04;
31:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=newIndex` (append is `C = u32::MAX`, see [`crate::APPEND`])
32:     pub const MOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x05;
33: }
34: 
35: /// Commands within the `PARAMETER` category.
36: pub mod parameter {
37:     /// `A=nodeId, B=(valueType << 16) | propertyId, C=value`
38:     pub const SET_PROPERTY: u8 = 0x01;
39:     /// `A=arenaRef (path), B=valueType (u8), C=value`
40:     pub const SET_DESIGN_TOKEN: u8 = 0x02;
41:     /// `A=nodeId, B=arenaRef (utf8)`
42:     pub const SET_TEXT: u8 = 0x03;
43:     /// **Draft.** `A=nodeId, B=days since epoch (I32), C=millis of day (U32)` —
44:     /// set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see
45:     /// `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` / `spec/OPCODE.md`.
46:     pub const SET_DATE: u8 = 0x04;
47: }
48: 
49: /// Commands within the `EVENT` category.
50: ///
51: /// Events are **raw inputs** (host → guest), each carrying a host-resolved
52: /// `targetId`. High-level interpretations (tap, drag, long-press) are built by
53: /// the guest/app from these raw inputs and are NOT part of the protocol.
54: pub mod event {
55:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
56:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u8 = 0x01;
57:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE`)
58:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u8 = 0x02;
59:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
60:     pub const POINTER_UP: u8 = 0x03;
61:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)` (Flags `KEY_REPEAT`)
62:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u8 = 0x04;
63:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)`
64:     pub const KEY_UP: u8 = 0x05;
65:     /// `A=targetId, B=value (f32)` — a control's value changed (host → guest).
66:     /// The renderer resolves the control's semantic value (e.g. a slider thumb
67:     /// dragged to a point on its track); the guest/app writes it into its state.
68:     pub const VALUE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x06;
69:     /// `A=targetId, B=string offset` — a text field's value changed (host →
70:     /// guest). The new text lives in the batch's string section, referenced by
71:     /// the *relative* offset in `B` (the same convention as `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`).
72:     pub const TEXT_CHANGED: u8 = 0x07;
73:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=focused (0/1)` — a node gained/lost focus.
74:     pub const FOCUS_CHANGED: u8 = 0x08;
75:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=editing (0/1)` — an editing session began/ended.
76:     pub const EDITING_CHANGED: u8 = 0x09;
77:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=0` — the user committed a field (onSubmit).
78:     pub const SUBMIT: u8 = 0x0A;
79:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=offsetX (f32), C=offsetY (f32)` — scroll offset.
80:     pub const SCROLL: u8 = 0x0B;
81:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=deltaX (f32), C=deltaY (f32)` — wheel/trackpad.
82:     pub const WHEEL: u8 = 0x0C;
83:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=days since epoch (I32), C=millis of day (U32)`
84:     /// — a `DATE_PICKER`'s value changed (matches `PARAMETER::SET_DATE`).
85:     pub const DATE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x0D;
86:     /// **Draft.** Global navigation request (host → guest), never node-keyed.
87:     /// With the `NAVIGATE_URL` flag, `B` is a string offset (event arena /
88:     /// batch string section) to the destination URL; without it, the event means
89:     /// "back one step" (native back affordance) and `B`/`C` are ignored.
90:     pub const NAVIGATE: u8 = 0x0E;
91:     /// **Draft.** A bound `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node's playback state changed
92:     /// (host → guest); `B` = 0/1. Reported only when `PLAYBACK_STATE` is bound.
93:     pub const MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x0F;
94:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node's current position (host → guest); `B` =
95:     /// seconds (f32). Reported while playing; an app-initiated seek is not echoed.
96:     pub const MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED: u8 = 0x10;
97:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node reached the end of its media (host → guest).
98:     pub const MEDIA_ENDED: u8 = 0x11;
99:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node's volume changed (host → guest); `B` =
100:     /// volume (f32, 0..1).
101:     pub const MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED: u8 = 0x12;
102: }
103: 
104: /// Commands within the `META` category.
105: pub mod meta {
106:     /// Host must clear all rendered output.
107:     pub const RESET: u8 = 0x01;
108:     /// `A=fieldId (u16, low), B=field value` — a platform environment field
109:     /// (host → guest); see [`crate::environment`]. An extensible field family:
110:     /// each opcode sets one field (viewport, initial route, …).
111:     pub const ENVIRONMENT: u8 = 0x02;
112:     /// The host (renderer) requests a full snapshot of the current tree
113:     /// (host → guest). `A/B/C = 0`. Used for reconnect/gap recovery.
114:     pub const RESYNC: u8 = 0x03;
115: }
116: 
117: /// Environment field ids for `META::ENVIRONMENT` (host → guest).
118: ///
119: /// Each opcode sets one platform environment field; new fields are new ids, never
120: /// new commands (spec/OPCODE.md §Environment fields).
121: pub mod environment {
122:     /// Viewport width in logical points (f32 in `B`).
123:     pub const VIEWPORT_WIDTH: u16 = 0x0001;
124:     /// Viewport height in logical points (f32 in `B`).
125:     pub const VIEWPORT_HEIGHT: u16 = 0x0002;
126:     /// The initial route/deep-link path (STRING: `B` is a string-section/event-arena
127:     /// offset — the `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` dual convention).
128:     pub const ROUTE: u16 = 0x0003;
129: }
130: 
131: /// Flag bits used across categories.
132: pub mod flag {
133:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` / `POINTER_UP`: secondary button (bit 0).
134:     pub const POINTER_SECONDARY: u16 = 0x0001;
135:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is entering/hovering (bit 0).
136:     pub const HOVER_ENTER: u16 = 0x0001;
137:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is leaving (bit 1).
138:     pub const HOVER_LEAVE: u16 = 0x0002;
139:     /// `KEY_DOWN`: key repeat (bit 1).
140:     pub const KEY_REPEAT: u16 = 0x0002;
141:     /// `NAVIGATE`: `B` is a URL string offset (bit 0). Without this flag the
142:     /// event is a back request.
143:     pub const NAVIGATE_URL: u16 = 0x0001;
144: }
145: 
146: /// Bits for the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (a u32 bitmask).
147: ///
148: /// Each bit requests that a renderer attach native input recognition for the
149: /// matching raw-input event and report it for that node — so any element (not
150: /// just a button) can emit raw events. Bits are independent of the `EVENT`
151: /// command ids; more event kinds can be added later.
152: pub mod listener {
153:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` events (bit 0).
154:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 0;
155:     /// `POINTER_MOVE` events (bit 1).
156:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u32 = 1 << 1;
157:     /// `POINTER_UP` events (bit 2).
158:     pub const POINTER_UP: u32 = 1 << 2;
159:     /// `KEY_DOWN` events (bit 3).
160:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 3;
161:     /// `KEY_UP` events (bit 4).
162:     pub const KEY_UP: u32 = 1 << 4;
163:     /// **Draft.** `FOCUS_CHANGED` events (bit 5).
164:     pub const FOCUS: u32 = 1 << 5;
165:     /// **Draft.** `EDITING_CHANGED` events (bit 6).
166:     pub const EDITING: u32 = 1 << 6;
167:     /// **Draft.** `SUBMIT` events (bit 7).
168:     pub const SUBMIT: u32 = 1 << 7;
169:     /// **Draft.** `SCROLL` events (bit 8).
170:     pub const SCROLL: u32 = 1 << 8;
171:     /// **Draft.** `WHEEL` events (bit 9).
172:     pub const WHEEL: u32 = 1 << 9;
173: 
174:     /// All pointer events (down + move + up).
175:     pub const POINTER: u32 = POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_MOVE | POINTER_UP;
176: }
177: 
178: /// Bits for the `BORDER_EDGES` style property (a u32 bitmask).
179: ///
180: /// Each bit selects one edge of a node's border. `LEADING`/`TRAILING` are
181: /// direction-aware; a renderer resolves them to physical `left`/`right`
182: /// according to its layout direction (LTR by default).
183: pub mod border_edges {
184:     /// Top edge (bit 0).
185:     pub const TOP: u32 = 1 << 0;
186:     /// Leading edge (bit 1) — physical left in LTR.
187:     pub const LEADING: u32 = 1 << 1;
188:     /// Bottom edge (bit 2).
189:     pub const BOTTOM: u32 = 1 << 2;
190:     /// Trailing edge (bit 3) — physical right in LTR.
191:     pub const TRAILING: u32 = 1 << 3;
192: 
193:     /// All four edges.
194:     pub const ALL: u32 = TOP | LEADING | BOTTOM | TRAILING;
195: }
196: 
197: /// Value types for `PARAMETER` properties (u8, encoded in the high byte of `B`).
198: pub mod value_type {
199:     pub const U8: u8 = 0x01;
200:     pub const U32: u8 = 0x02;
201:     pub const I32: u8 = 0x03;
202:     pub const F32: u8 = 0x04;
203:     pub const STRING: u8 = 0x05;
204:     pub const ENUM: u8 = 0x06;
205:     pub const COLOR: u8 = 0x07;
206:     pub const DESIGN_TOKEN: u8 = 0x08;
207: }
208: 
209: /// Component types (u16, encoded in the low half of `B` of `TREE::CREATE_NODE`).
210: ///
211: /// IDs are grouped into three definitive ranges (see `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`):
212: /// Primitive Drawing `0x01`–`0x0F`, Layout & Container `0x10`–`0x1F`, Semantic
213: /// Control `0x20`–`0x2F`, plus the utility `COMMENT` at `0x7F`. Renumbered
214: /// pre-release (wire version stays 1).
215: pub mod component_type {
216:     // ── Primitive Drawing & Visual Nodes (0x01–0x0F) ────────────────────────
217:     /// Standard styled text display.
218:     pub const TEXT: u16 = 0x01;
219:     /// Raster, vector, or system icon asset.
220:     pub const IMAGE: u16 = 0x02;
221:     /// **Draft.** Solid color / layout-filling background view.
222:     pub const COLOR: u16 = 0x03;
223:     /// **Draft.** Vector geometry (`SHAPE_KIND` selects the shape).
224:     pub const SHAPE: u16 = 0x04;
225:     /// **Draft.** Axis-aligned separator line.
226:     pub const DIVIDER: u16 = 0x05;
227:     /// Flexible expanding layout filler.

537: /// The protocol value type for a property id.
538: ///
539: /// Color-valued properties (COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_COLOR) are emitted
540: /// with the `COLOR` value type; `EVENT_LISTENERS` and `BORDER_EDGES` are raw
541: /// `U32` bitmasks; `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY` are `STRING`; `LINE_LIMIT`,
542: /// `ACTION_ID`, and `BINDING_ID` are `U32`; all other constraint/style
543: /// properties are `F32` (enum-valued properties like `ALIGNMENT`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`
544: /// carry their numeric code as an `F32`). See `spec/MODIFIERS.md` for the
545: /// canonical mapping.
546: pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
547:     match prop {
548:         property_id::COLOR
549:         | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
550:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR
551:         | property_id::COLOR_VALUE
552:         | property_id::COLOR_MULTIPLY
553:         | property_id::SHADOW_COLOR
554:         | property_id::TINT => value_type::COLOR,
555:         property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS | property_id::BORDER_EDGES => value_type::U32,
556:         property_id::SELECTED
557:         | property_id::IS_SECURE
558:         | property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE
559:         | property_id::VISIBLE
560:         | property_id::ENABLED
561:         | property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS
562:         | property_id::UNDERLINE
563:         | property_id::STRIKETHROUGH
564:         | property_id::COLOR_INVERT
565:         | property_id::ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING
566:         | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL
567:         | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL => value_type::U8,
568:         property_id::LABEL
569:         | property_id::PROMPT
570:         | property_id::FONT_FAMILY
571:         | property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE
572:         | property_id::AUDIO_SOURCE
573:         | property_id::VIDEO_SOURCE
574:         | property_id::ROUTE => value_type::STRING,
575:         property_id::LINE_LIMIT
576:         | property_id::SELECTION
577:         | property_id::ACTION_ID
578:         | property_id::BINDING_ID
579:         | property_id::NAV_DEPTH => value_type::U32,
580:         _ => value_type::F32,
581:     }
582: }

449:         let text = crate::arena::get_str(event_arena, op.b()).ok()?;

1: //! Producer-side ring helpers operating on the ring region and header cursors.
2: //!
3: //! The ring is a power-of-two slot array. The guest writes at `writeCursor` and
4: //! the host reads from `readCursor`. Both cursors live in the header block.
5: 
6: use alloc::vec::Vec;
7: 
8: use crate::opcode::Opcode;
9: use crate::{constants, memory, memory::header};
10: 
11: /// Errors produced by the ring producer.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum RingError {
14:     /// The ring is full (consumer has not caught up). The producer SHOULD
15:     /// publish a frame before emitting further opcodes.
16:     Full,
17: }
18: 
19: /// Append `op` to the ring at `writeCursor` and advance the cursor.
20: ///
21: /// `slots` is the full ring region; `mask` wraps the cursor. Fails with
22: /// `RingError::Full` when the next slot equals `readCursor`.
23: #[inline]
24: pub(crate) fn push(slots: &mut [u8], header: &mut [u8], mask: usize, op: &Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
25:     let write = cursor(header, memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
26:     let next = (write + 1) & mask;
27:     if next == cursor(header, memory::OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask) {
28:         return Err(RingError::Full);
29:     }
30:     let bytes = op.to_bytes();
31:     let off = write * Opcode::SIZE;
32:     slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].copy_from_slice(&bytes);
33:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, next as u32);
34:     Ok(())
35: }
36: 
37: /// Read the current cursor value for a header offset, masked.
38: #[inline]
39: pub(crate) fn cursor(header: &[u8], off: usize, mask: usize) -> usize {
40:     header::get_u32(header, off) as usize & mask
41: }

211: /// Append an `EVENT`-category opcode to the host → guest event ring.
212: ///
213: /// The host (renderer) writes at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest reads from
214: /// `eventReadCursor`. Same 16-byte slot layout as the guest → host ring.
215: #[inline]
216: pub(crate) fn push_event(
217:     event_slots: &mut [u8],
218:     header: &mut [u8],
219:     mask: usize,
220:     op: &Opcode,
221: ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
222:     let write = cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
223:     let next = (write + 1) & mask;
224:     if next == cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_READ_CURSOR, mask) {
225:         return Err(RingError::Full);
226:     }
227:     let bytes = op.to_bytes();
228:     let off = write * Opcode::SIZE;
229:     event_slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].copy_from_slice(&bytes);
230:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_WRITE_CURSOR, next as u32);
231:     Ok(())
232: }
233: 
234: /// Drain all pending `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
235: /// advancing `eventReadCursor`. The guest (app/engine) reads raw inputs here.
236: #[inline]
237: pub(crate) fn read_events(
238:     event_slots: &[u8],
239:     header: &mut [u8],
240:     mask: usize,
241: ) -> Vec<Opcode> {
242:     let read = cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_READ_CURSOR, mask);
243:     let write = cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
244:     // The POC host never lets the event ring wrap past the reader; drain only a
245:     // contiguous (unwrapped) run.
246:     if write < read {
247:         return Vec::new();
248:     }
249:     let count = write - read;
250:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
251:     for i in 0..count {
252:         let slot = (read + i) & mask;
253:         let off = slot * Opcode::SIZE;
254:         let bytes: [u8; Opcode::SIZE] =
255:             event_slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap();
256:         out.push(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes));
257:     }
258:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_READ_CURSOR, write as u32);
259:     out
260: }

1: //! Bump arena for variable-length data in linear memory.
2: //!
3: //! Every entry is self-describing: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`. Opcodes
4: //! reference entries by their byte offset (`arenaRef`), so the entry length is
5: //! read directly from the arena and every opcode stays 16 bytes.
6: 
7: use crate::memory::header;
8: 
9: /// Errors produced by the arena.
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11: pub enum ArenaError {
12:     /// Not enough remaining bytes for the allocation.
13:     OutOfSpace,
14:     /// The arena offset is out of bounds or points to an invalid entry.
15:     InvalidOffset,
16: }
17: 
18: /// Allocate `bytes` into the arena region, returning its byte offset.
19: ///
20: /// The cursor lives in the header block (`OFF_ARENA_CURSOR`).
21: #[inline]
22: pub(crate) fn alloc(data: &mut [u8], header: &mut [u8], bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
23:     alloc_at(data, header, crate::memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR, bytes)
24: }
25: 
26: /// Allocate `bytes` into the host → guest (event) arena region, returning its
27: /// byte offset. The cursor lives in the header block
28: /// (`OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR`, host-owned) — the host writes event string
29: /// payloads here so the guest can resolve them over the shared ring.
30: #[inline]
31: pub(crate) fn alloc_event(
32:     data: &mut [u8],
33:     header: &mut [u8],
34:     bytes: &[u8],
35: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
36:     alloc_at(data, header, crate::memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, bytes)
37: }
38: 
39: /// Allocate into any arena region, using the given header cursor offset.
40: #[inline]
41: pub(crate) fn alloc_at(
42:     data: &mut [u8],
43:     header: &mut [u8],
44:     cursor_off: usize,
45:     bytes: &[u8],
46: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
47:     let cursor = header::get_u32(header, cursor_off) as usize;
48:     let len = bytes.len();
49:     let needed = 4 + len;
50:     if cursor + needed > data.len() {
51:         return Err(ArenaError::OutOfSpace);
52:     }
53:     data[cursor..cursor + 4].copy_from_slice(&(len as u32).to_le_bytes());
54:     data[cursor + 4..cursor + needed].copy_from_slice(bytes);
55:     header::set_u32(header, cursor_off, (cursor + needed) as u32);
56:     Ok(cursor as u32)
57: }
58: 
59: /// Allocate a string, returning its arena offset.
60: #[inline]
61: pub(crate) fn alloc_str(
62:     data: &mut [u8],
63:     header: &mut [u8],
64:     s: &str,
65: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
66:     alloc(data, header, s.as_bytes())
67: }
68: 
69: /// Read the bytes of the entry at `offset` from an arena region.
70: #[inline]
71: pub(crate) fn get(data: &[u8], offset: u32) -> Result<&[u8], ArenaError> {
72:     let off = offset as usize;
73:     if off + 4 > data.len() {
74:         return Err(ArenaError::InvalidOffset);
75:     }
76:     let len = u32::from_le_bytes(data[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
77:     if off + 4 + len > data.len() {
78:         return Err(ArenaError::InvalidOffset);
79:     }
80:     Ok(&data[off + 4..off + 4 + len])
81: }
82: 
83: /// Read the string at `offset` (UTF-8 validated).
84: #[inline]
85: pub(crate) fn get_str(data: &[u8], offset: u32) -> Result<&str, ArenaError> {
86:     let bytes = get(data, offset)?;
87:     core::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| ArenaError::InvalidOffset)
88: }
89:

91: mod tests {
92:     use alloc::vec;
93:     use super::*;
94:     use crate::memory::{header, MemoryLayout};
95: 
96:     #[test]
97:     fn alloc_and_get_round_trip() {
98:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();

159: /// Producer side: the guest engine writing opcodes and arena data into shared
160: /// linear memory. Owns the header, ring, and arena regions as disjoint slices.
161: pub struct Guest<'a> {
162:     header: &'a mut [u8],
163:     slots: &'a mut [u8],
164:     /// Host → guest event ring (guest reads raw inputs here).
165:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
166:     arena: &'a mut [u8],
167:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the guest resolves `TEXT_CHANGED`
168:     /// text here over the shared ring).
169:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
170:     /// Write cursor captured at `begin_frame`.
171:     frame_start: u32,
172: }
173: 
174: impl<'a> Guest<'a> {
175:     /// Create a guest view over the linear memory. `init_memory` MUST have been
176:     /// called on the same memory beforehand.
177:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
178:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
179:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
180:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
181:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
182:         let frame_start = header::get_u32(header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
183:         Self {
184:             header,
185:             slots,
186:             event_slots,
187:             arena,
188:             event_arena,
189:             frame_start,
190:         }
191:     }
192: 
193:     fn mask(&self) -> usize {
194:         slot_mask(self.header)
195:     }
196: 
197:     /// Record the start of a new frame.
198:     pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
199:         self.frame_start = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
200:     }
201: 
202:     /// Number of opcodes written since the last `begin_frame`.
203:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
204:         let write = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
205:         let mask = self.mask() as u32;
206:         (write.wrapping_sub(self.frame_start) & mask) as usize
207:     }
208: 
209:     /// End the frame: increments `frameCount`.
210:     pub fn end_frame(&mut self) {
211:         let count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
212:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, count.wrapping_add(1));
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// Total frames produced so far.
216:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
217:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
218:     }
219: 
220:     // --- TREE ---
221: 
222:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, node_id: u32, component_type: u16) -> Result<(), RingError> {
223:         ring_fn::push_create_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, component_type)
224:     }
225: 
226:     pub fn delete_node(&mut self, node_id: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
227:         ring_fn::push_delete_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id)
228:     }
229: 
230:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
231:         ring_fn::push_insert_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, index)
232:     }
233: 
234:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
235:         ring_fn::push_remove_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child)
236:     }
237: 
238:     pub fn move_child(
239:         &mut self,
240:         parent: u32,
241:         child: u32,
242:         new_index: u32,
243:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
244:         ring_fn::push_move_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, new_index)
245:     }
246: 
247:     // --- Raw opcode push (guest → host) ---
248: 
249:     /// Push a caller-built raw opcode into the ring. This is the escape hatch
250:     /// for foreign hosts (C ABI / FFM) that construct the 16-byte opcode
251:     /// themselves and write it into the shared ring in place.
252:     pub fn push_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
253:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
254:     }
255: 
256:     // --- STYLE ---
257: 
258:     pub fn set_property(
259:         &mut self,
260:         node_id: u32,
261:         property_id: u16,
262:         value_type: u8,
263:         value: u32,
264:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
265:         ring_fn::push_set_property(
266:             self.slots,
267:             self.header,
268:             self.mask(),
269:             node_id,
270:             property_id,
271:             value_type,
272:             value,
273:         )
274:     }
275: 
276:     /// Set a node's text content via the arena.
277:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, node_id: u32, text: &str) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
278:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, text).map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
279:         ring_fn::push_set_text(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, arena_ref)?;
280:         Ok(arena_ref)
281:     }
282: 
283:     /// Set a node's date value via `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` (draft): `days` since the
284:     /// epoch (I32, pre-1970 negative) and `millis` of day (U32, 0..86,400,000).
285:     pub fn set_date(&mut self, node_id: u32, days: i32, millis: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
286:         let op = Opcode::new(
287:             category::PARAMETER,
288:             crate::parameter::SET_DATE,
289:             0,
290:             node_id,
291:             days as u32,
292:             millis,
293:         );
294:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
295:     }
296: 
297:     /// Override a design token globally via `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`:
298:     /// `path` (arena string) → `value` of `value_type`. Applies everywhere the
299:     /// renderer resolves tokens (spec/TOKENS.md). A `dark.`-prefixed path
300:     /// overrides the dark variant. Returns the arena offset of the path.
301:     pub fn set_design_token(
302:         &mut self,
303:         path: &str,
304:         value_type: u8,
305:         value: u32,
306:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
307:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, path)
308:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
309:         let op = Opcode::new(
310:             category::PARAMETER,
311:             crate::parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN,
312:             0,
313:             arena_ref,
314:             u32::from(value_type),
315:             value,
316:         );
317:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)?;
318:         Ok(arena_ref)
319:     }
320: 
321:     /// Override a design token with a **STRING value** via `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
322:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md): both the token path and the value are arena strings —
323:     /// `A` = path ref, `B` = `STRING` value type, `C` = value ref. Returns the
324:     /// arena offset of the path.
325:     pub fn set_design_token_string(
326:         &mut self,
327:         path: &str,
328:         value: &str,
329:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
330:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, path)
331:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
332:         let value_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, value)
333:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
334:         let op = Opcode::new(
335:             category::PARAMETER,
336:             crate::parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN,
337:             0,
338:             arena_ref,
339:             u32::from(crate::value_type::STRING),
340:             value_ref,
341:         );
342:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)?;
343:         Ok(arena_ref)
344:     }
345: 
346:     /// Allocate arbitrary bytes into the arena, returning the offset.
347:     pub fn alloc(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
348:         arena_fn::alloc(self.arena, self.header, bytes)
349:     }
350: 
351:     /// Allocate a string into the arena, returning the offset.
352:     pub fn alloc_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
353:         arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, s)
354:     }
355: 
356:     // --- META ---
357: 
358:     pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<(), RingError> {
359:         ring_fn::push_reset(self.slots, self.header, self.mask())
360:     }
361: 
362:     // --- EVENT ingress (host → guest) ---
363: 
364:     /// Drain all pending raw-input events written by the host into the event
365:     /// ring, decoding each 16-byte `EVENT` opcode into a typed [`Event`].
366:     ///
367:     /// The guest (app/engine) polls this to receive renderer-reported inputs.
368:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<Event> {
369:         let mask = self.mask();
370:         let ops = ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask);
371:         ops.into_iter()
372:             .filter_map(|op| crate::events::decode_event(&op, self.event_arena))
373:             .collect()
374:     }
375: 
376:     /// Drain raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring as
377:     /// their 16-byte wire form (no decoding). Used by foreign hosts that want
378:     /// the raw bytes.
379:     pub fn drain_event_opcodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Opcode> {
380:         let mask = self.mask();
381:         ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask)
382:     }
383: 
384:     /// The host → guest event arena bump cursor (diagnostics/tests).
385:     pub fn event_arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
386:         header::get_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR)
387:     }
388: 
389:     /// Push a raw `EVENT`-category opcode into the host → guest event ring.
390:     ///
391:     /// This is the host-side write (the renderer reporting an input). Exposed
392:     /// here (guest can hold the ring too) so a C-ABI shim can inject raw event
393:     /// opcodes without round-tripping through the typed [`Event`] enum.
394:     pub fn push_event_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
395:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
396:     }
397: }
398: 
399: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
400: // Host (consumer)
401: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
402: 
403: /// A completed frame produced by the guest: a sequence of opcodes plus arena
404: /// access.
405: ///
406: /// `Frame` is the **transport seam**: both the shared-memory ring (`Host`) and
407: /// network batch decoders produce frame views, so consumers such as
408: /// `RenderTree::apply_frame` work identically regardless of origin.
409: pub struct Frame<'a> {
410:     slots: &'a [u8],
411:     arena: &'a [u8],
412:     start: usize,
413:     end: usize,
414: }
415: 
416: impl<'a> Frame<'a> {
417:     /// Construct a frame view over contiguous 16-byte opcode slots plus an
418:     /// arena region (`start`/`end` are byte offsets into `slots`).
419:     ///
420:     /// Used by transport backends to produce `Frame` views over their own
421:     /// buffers; `Host` builds these internally from the ring.
422:     pub fn from_parts(slots: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
423:         Self {
424:             slots,
425:             arena,
426:             start,
427:             end,
428:         }
429:     }
430: 
431:     /// Iterate the opcodes in this frame, in order.
432:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> FrameIter<'a> {
433:         FrameIter {
434:             slots: self.slots,
435:             cursor: self.start,
436:             end: self.end,
437:         }
438:     }
439: 
440:     /// Number of opcodes in the frame.
441:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
442:         (self.end - self.start) / Opcode::SIZE
443:     }
444: 
445:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
446:         self.len() == 0
447:     }
448: 
449:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Guest::alloc` / `Guest::alloc_str`).
450:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], ArenaError> {
451:         arena_fn::get(self.arena, offset)
452:     }
453: 
454:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
455:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, ArenaError> {
456:         arena_fn::get_str(self.arena, offset)
457:     }
458: 
459:     /// The full arena region (for transport serialization of arena deltas).
460:     pub fn arena(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
461:         self.arena
462:     }
463: }
464: 
465: /// Iterator over the opcodes in a `Frame`.
466: pub struct FrameIter<'a> {
467:     slots: &'a [u8],
468:     cursor: usize,
469:     end: usize,
470: }
471: 
472: impl<'a> Iterator for FrameIter<'a> {
473:     type Item = Opcode;
474: 
475:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Opcode> {
476:         if self.cursor >= self.end {
477:             return None;
478:         }
479:         let bytes: [u8; 16] = self.slots[self.cursor..self.cursor + 16].try_into().unwrap();
480:         self.cursor += 16;
481:         Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes))
482:     }
483: }
484: 
485: /// Consumer side: the host renderer reading completed frames.
486: ///
487: /// SPSC contract: the host never reads past the producer's published
488: /// `writeCursor`, and the producer never overwrites an unconsumed `readCursor`.
489: /// If the host is slow, multiple produced frames are coalesced into one `Frame`
490: /// (opcodes remain in order); the `frameCount` simply signals "new data".
491: pub struct Host<'a> {
492:     header: &'a mut [u8],
493:     slots: &'a [u8],
494:     /// Host → guest event ring (host writes raw inputs here).
495:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
496:     arena: &'a [u8],
497:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the host writes event string
498:     /// payloads here, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED` text over the shared ring).
499:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
500:     /// Number of frames already consumed by this host view.
501:     consumed: u32,
502: }
503: 
504: impl<'a> Host<'a> {
505:     /// Create a host view over the linear memory.
506:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
507:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
508:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
509:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
510:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
511:         let slots: &'a [u8] = slots;
512:         let arena: &'a [u8] = arena;
513:         Self {
514:             header,
515:             slots,
516:             event_slots,
517:             arena,
518:             event_arena,
519:             consumed: 0,
520:         }
521:     }
522: 
523:     /// Total frames produced by the guest (for diagnostics).
524:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
525:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
526:     }
527: 
528:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
529:     ///
530:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
531:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
532:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
533:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
534:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
535:             return Vec::new();
536:         }
537:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
538:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
539:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
540: 
541:         // The POC producer flushes before the ring fills, so `end >= start`
542:         // always holds. Guard against a wrapped ring by draining nothing; a
543:         // wrapped producer must flush first (see OPCODE.md backpressure).
544:         if end < start {
545:             return Vec::new();
546:         }
547: 
548:         // No new opcodes since the last drain (readCursor == writeCursor). This
549:         // also covers a freshly-created host view whose `consumed` counter
550:         // starts at 0 but whose cursors have already been drained by an earlier
551:         // view — without this, `next_frame` would return empty frames forever.
552:         if start == end {
553:             return Vec::new();
554:         }
555: 
556:         let frames = vec![Frame {
557:             slots: self.slots,
558:             arena: self.arena,
559:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
560:             end: end * Opcode::SIZE,
561:         }];
562: 
563:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, end as u32);
564:         self.consumed = frame_count;
565: 
566:         // A `META::RESET` invalidates prior state: reset the host → guest event
567:         // arena cursor so the host starts bump-allocating fresh (matching the
568:         // guest arena's reset-on-RESET semantics).
569:         let reset_seen = self.slots[start * Opcode::SIZE..end * Opcode::SIZE]
570:             .chunks_exact(Opcode::SIZE)
571:             .any(|slot| {
572:                 let bytes: [u8; 16] = slot.try_into().unwrap();
573:                 let op = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
574:                 op.category() == category::META && op.command() == crate::meta::RESET
575:             });
576:         if reset_seen {
577:             memory::header::set_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, 0);
578:         }
579: 
580:         frames
581:     }
582: 
583:     /// Write a raw-input event (host → guest) into the event ring, encoded as a
584:     /// 16-byte `EVENT` opcode. The renderer reports inputs here; the guest
585:     /// drains them via [`Guest::drain_events`].
586:     ///
587:     /// `TextChanged` text and `Navigate` URLs are bump-allocated into the
588:     /// host → guest **event arena** and referenced by their absolute offset in
589:     /// `B` (the `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention); the guest resolves them
590:     /// from the same region. If the event arena is full the event is rejected
591:     /// with [`RingError::Full`] (backpressure).
592:     pub fn send_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), RingError> {
593:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
594:         let op = match event {
595:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
596:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, value.as_bytes())
597:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
598:                 Opcode::new(category::EVENT, crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED, 0, *target, offset, 0)
599:             }
600:             Event::Navigate { url: Some(url) } => {
601:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, url.as_bytes())
602:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
603:                 Opcode::new(
604:                     category::EVENT,
605:                     crate::event::NAVIGATE,
606:                     crate::flag::NAVIGATE_URL,
607:                     0,
608:                     offset,
609:                     0,
610:                 )
611:             }
612:             _ => event.encode(),
613:         };
614:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, mask, &op)
615:     }
616: }

228: /// Assign stable unique sequential ids to a tree (pre-order; root first).
229: ///
230: /// The engine keys its diff snapshot by node id, so call this after building
231: /// the (possibly re-built) tree and before `Engine::emit`.
232: pub fn assign_ids(root: &mut Node, next: &mut u32) {
233:     root.id = *next;
234:     *next += 1;
235:     for child in &mut root.children {
236:         assign_ids(child, next);
237:     }
238: }

243: /// keys the recognizer's tap target to the closure registered by
244: /// `.on_tap_gesture(...)`.
245: pub fn collect_tap_handlers(
246:     root: &Node,
247:     out: &mut BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>,
248: ) {
249:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
250:         let Gesture::Tap(handler) = gesture;
251:         out.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
252:     }
253:     for child in &root.children {
254:         collect_tap_handlers(child, out);

1: //! Reactive signals (Angular-style).
2: //!
3: //! A [`Signal`] is a piece of application state owned by the engine. Retained
4: //! tree nodes bind their text or a property to a signal via [`SignalId`]; the
5: //! engine records those dependencies during emission, so when a signal's value
6: //! changes, only the nodes that read it re-emit their deltas.
7: //!
8: //! Signals live here (in `no_std` core) so any host — Rust, the native C ABI,
9: //! a future WASM/browser guest — shares the same reactive runtime.
10: 
11: use alloc::string::String;
12: use alloc::vec::Vec;
13: 
14: /// A signal's value: one of the protocol value kinds.
15: ///
16: /// Property bindings pack to a `SET_PROPERTY` value (u32); text bindings use
17: /// [`SignalValue::Str`]. The richer kinds (`Bool`, `Enum`) are ergonomic typing
18: /// at the host boundary — they still collapse onto the wire's `u32` value.
19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
20: pub enum SignalValue {
21:     /// A float property (spacing, font_size, padding, opacity, size hints…).
22:     F32(f32),
23:     /// A raw u32 property (color `0xAARRGGBB`, an `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask, …).
24:     U32(u32),
25:     /// A boolean property (visible, clips_to_bounds, …).
26:     Bool(bool),
27:     /// An enum property wire value (alignment, text alignment, truncation, …).
28:     Enum(u8),
29:     /// A string (text content, font family).
30:     Str(String),
31: }
32: 
33: impl SignalValue {
34:     /// Pack this value as a `SET_PROPERTY` `u32` value. `None` for [`Str`],
35:     /// which is only valid for text bindings.
36:     pub fn to_property_u32(&self) -> Option<u32> {
37:         match self {
38:             SignalValue::F32(f) => Some(f.to_bits()),
39:             SignalValue::U32(u) => Some(*u),
40:             SignalValue::Bool(b) => Some(if *b { 1.0f32 } else { 0.0f32 }.to_bits()),
41:             SignalValue::Enum(e) => Some((*e as f32).to_bits()),
42:             SignalValue::Str(_) => None,
43:         }
44:     }
45: 
46:     /// The text for a text binding. `None` for non-`Str` values.
47:     pub fn to_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
48:         match self {
49:             SignalValue::Str(s) => Some(s.as_str()),
50:             _ => None,
51:         }
52:     }
53: }
54: 
55: /// A stable, non-generic handle to a signal (an index into the engine's
56: /// [`SignalStore`]). This is the FFI-safe handle handed to foreign hosts.
57: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
58: pub struct SignalId(pub u32);
59: 
60: /// A dependency: a node binding that reads a signal.
61: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
62: pub enum Dep {
63:     /// The node's text is bound to the signal.
64:     Text { node: u32 },
65:     /// A node property is bound to the signal.
66:     Property { node: u32, prop: u16 },
67: }
68: 
69: #[derive(Debug)]
70: struct SignalCell {
71:     value: SignalValue,
72:     /// Reverse dependency index: the node bindings that read this signal.
73:     deps: Vec<Dep>,
74: }
75: 
76: /// Owns signal storage plus the reverse dependency index (`signal -> deps`).
77: ///
78: /// The engine rebuilds the index during each full emit; between emits, the
79: /// index lets `set` find exactly the nodes that depend on a changed signal.
80: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
81: pub struct SignalStore {
82:     cells: Vec<SignalCell>,
83: }
84: 
85: impl SignalStore {
86:     /// Create a new signal with an initial value, returning its handle.
87:     pub fn create(&mut self, value: SignalValue) -> SignalId {
88:         let id = SignalId(self.cells.len() as u32);
89:         self.cells.push(SignalCell {
90:             value,
91:             deps: Vec::new(),
92:         });
93:         id
94:     }
95: 
96:     /// Replace a signal's value. Returns `true` if the value actually changed.
97:     pub fn set(&mut self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> bool {
98:         if let Some(cell) = self.cells.get_mut(id.0 as usize) {
99:             if cell.value != value {
100:                 cell.value = value;
101:                 return true;
102:             }
103:         }
104:         false
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Read a signal's current value.
108:     pub fn get(&self, id: SignalId) -> Option<&SignalValue> {
109:         self.cells.get(id.0 as usize).map(|c| &c.value)
110:     }
111: 
112:     /// The dependencies recorded for a signal (empty if none).
113:     pub fn deps(&self, id: SignalId) -> &[Dep] {
114:         self.cells
115:             .get(id.0 as usize)
116:             .map(|c| c.deps.as_slice())
117:             .unwrap_or(&[])
118:     }
119: 
120:     /// Clear all recorded dependencies (called at the start of a full emit).
121:     pub fn clear_deps(&mut self) {
122:         for cell in &mut self.cells {
123:             cell.deps.clear();
124:         }
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Record a dependency for a signal.
128:     pub fn add_dep(&mut self, id: SignalId, dep: Dep) {
129:         if let Some(cell) = self.cells.get_mut(id.0 as usize) {
130:             if !cell.deps.contains(&dep) {
131:                 cell.deps.push(dep);
132:             }
133:         }
134:     }
135: 
136:     /// Number of signals allocated (diagnostics).
137:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
138:         self.cells.len()
139:     }
140: 
141:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
142:         self.cells.is_empty()
143:     }
144: }

2: //!
3: //! The engine holds the application's retained view tree and emits the
4: //! declarative structure as `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
5: //! buffer (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment). It does not
6: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers lay out their own elements.
7: //!
8: //! Emission is diff-based: on each `emit` the engine compares the current tree
9: //! against a snapshot of what it last emitted and writes only the opcodes for
10: //! nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
11: //!
12: //! The emit pass performs zero dynamic heap allocations in the steady state.
13: //!
14: //! ## Signals
15: //!
16: //! Nodes may bind their text or a property to a [`crate::SignalId`]. The engine
17: //! resolves those bindings during emit (recording the dependency) and re-emits
18: //! only the affected nodes on [`Engine::set_signal`] — no full tree walk.
19: 
20: use alloc::borrow::ToOwned;
21: use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;
22: use alloc::string::{String, ToString};
23: use alloc::vec::Vec;
24: 
25: use pathland_core::{value_type, value_type_for};
26: use pathland_core::Guest;
27: 
28: use crate::node::{component_type_id, Component, Node};
29: use crate::signal::{Dep, SignalId, SignalStore, SignalValue};
30: 
31: /// Per-node state the engine remembers from the last emission.
32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
33: struct SnapshotNode {
34:     component_type: u16,
35:     parent: Option<u32>,
36:     index: usize,
37:     text: Option<String>,
38:     properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
39:     /// Last-emitted `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs: property → (token path, arena offset).
40:     /// The arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged ref never
41:     /// re-allocates into the bump arena.
42:     token_refs: BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>,
43:     /// Generation stamp set on each emit pass; used to detect deleted nodes.
44:     gen: u64,
45: }
46: 
47: /// Result of an emission pass.
48: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
49: pub struct EmitResult {
50:     /// Number of opcodes written to the ring.
51:     pub opcodes: usize,
52: }
53: 
54: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
55: ///
56: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted and owns the signal
57: /// store. Calling `emit` with a (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only
58: /// the delta opcodes; `set_signal` writes deltas for only the bound nodes.
59: pub struct Engine {
60:     /// nodeId to last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
61:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
62:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
63:     gen: u64,
64:     /// Reactive signal store (owns values + the reverse dependency index).
65:     store: SignalStore,
66: }
67: 
68: impl Default for Engine {
69:     fn default() -> Self {
70:         Self::new()
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: impl Engine {
75:     pub fn new() -> Self {
76:         Self {
77:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
78:             gen: 0,
79:             store: SignalStore::default(),
80:         }
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
84:     pub fn emit(
85:         &mut self,
86:         root: &Node,
87:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
88:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_core::RingError> {
89:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
90:         // Rebuild the signal dependency index from scratch; reconcile re-adds
91:         // the bindings this tree actually uses, so stale subscriptions vanish.
92:         self.store.clear_deps();
93:         let mut out = 0usize;
94:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
95: 
96:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
97:             if let Some(s) = slot {
98:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
99:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
100:                     out += 1;
101:                     *slot = None;
102:                 }
103:             }
104:         }
105:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
109:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {
110:         self.snapshot.iter().filter(|s| s.is_some()).count()
111:     }
112: 
113:     /// Emit a global design-token override (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`).
114:     /// Overrides are renderer-global and apply everywhere the renderer resolves
115:     /// tokens; a `dark.`-prefixed path overrides the dark variant
116:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md). Returns the arena offset of the token path.
117:     pub fn set_design_token(
118:         &mut self,
119:         path: &str,
120:         value_type: u8,
121:         value: u32,
122:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
123:     ) -> Result<u32, pathland_core::RingError> {
124:         guest.set_design_token(path, value_type, value)
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Emit a batch of global design-token overrides ([`Theme`](crate::Theme))
128:     /// as `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes. `STRING`-valued overrides allocate
129:     /// their value into the guest arena first (the wire carries an arena ref).
130:     ///
131:     /// Overrides are renderer-global: they never re-emit nodes and are not part
132:     /// of the diff. Emit once at mount, before the tree.
133:     pub fn apply_theme(
134:         &mut self,
135:         theme: &crate::Theme,
136:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
137:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
138:         for (path, value) in theme.iter() {
139:             self.emit_token_override(path, value, guest)?;
140:         }
141:         Ok(())
142:     }
143: 
144:     /// Emit an adaptive theme ([`AdaptiveTheme`](crate::AdaptiveTheme)): the
145:     /// **light** theme's overrides as base tokens, the **dark** theme's with the
146:     /// `dark.` scheme prefix (spec/TOKENS.md).
147:     pub fn apply_adaptive_theme(
148:         &mut self,
149:         adaptive: &crate::AdaptiveTheme,
150:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
151:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
152:         self.apply_theme(&adaptive.light, guest)?;
153:         for (path, value) in adaptive.dark.iter() {
154:             let dark_path = if path.starts_with("dark.") {
155:                 path.to_string()
156:             } else {
157:                 alloc::format!("dark.{path}")
158:             };
159:             self.emit_token_override(&dark_path, value, guest)?;
160:         }
161:         Ok(())
162:     }
163: 
164:     /// Emit one `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override, arena-allocating STRING values.
165:     fn emit_token_override(
166:         &mut self,
167:         path: &str,
168:         value: &pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue,
169:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
170:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
171:         use pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue;
172:         match value {
173:             TokenValue::Str(s) => {
174:                 let ref_ = guest
175:                     .alloc_str(s)
176:                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
177:                 guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), ref_)?;
178:             }
179:             _ => {
180:                 if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
181:                     guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), bits)?;
182:                 }
183:             }
184:         }
185:         Ok(())
186:     }
187: 
188:     // --- Signals ---
189: 
190:     /// Create a new signal with an initial value.
191:     pub fn create_signal(&mut self, value: SignalValue) -> SignalId {
192:         self.store.create(value)
193:     }
194: 
195:     /// Read a signal's current value.
196:     pub fn get_signal(&self, id: SignalId) -> Option<&SignalValue> {
197:         self.store.get(id)
198:     }
199: 
200:     /// Replace a signal's value and re-emit only the nodes that depend on it.
201:     ///
202:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas for the bound nodes whose
203:     /// materialized value changed. Returns the number of opcodes written.
204:     pub fn set_signal(
205:         &mut self,
206:         id: SignalId,
207:         value: SignalValue,
208:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
209:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
210:         if !self.store.set(id, value) {
211:             return Ok(0);
212:         }
213:         let mut out = 0usize;
214:         let deps: Vec<Dep> = self.store.deps(id).to_vec();
215:         for dep in deps {
216:             match dep {
217:                 Dep::Text { node } => {
218:                     let new_text: Option<String> = self
219:                         .store
220:                         .get(id)
221:                         .and_then(SignalValue::to_text)
222:                         .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
223:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_text(node);
224:                     if new_text.as_deref() != prev_text {
225:                         if let Some(t) = new_text.as_deref() {
226:                             guest.set_text(node, t)?;
227:                             out += 1;
228:                         }
229:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
230:                             s.text = new_text;
231:                         }
232:                     }
233:                 }
234:                 Dep::Property { node, prop } => {
235:                     let new_value = self
236:                         .store
237:                         .get(id)
238:                         .and_then(SignalValue::to_property_u32);
239:                     let prev_value = self.snapshot_property(node, prop);
240:                     if new_value != prev_value {
241:                         if let Some(v) = new_value {
242:                             guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type_for(prop), v)?;
243:                             out += 1;
244:                         }
245:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
246:                             match new_value {
247:                                 Some(v) => {
248:                                     s.properties.insert(prop, v);
249:                                 }
250:                                 None => {
251:                                     s.properties.remove(&prop);
252:                                 }
253:                             }
254:                         }
255:                     }
256:                 }
257:             }
258:         }
259:         Ok(out)
260:     }
261: 
262:     fn snapshot_mut(&mut self, node: u32) -> Option<&mut SnapshotNode> {
263:         self.snapshot
264:             .get_mut(node as usize)
265:             .and_then(|s| s.as_mut())
266:     }
267: 
268:     fn snapshot_text(&self, node: u32) -> Option<&str> {
269:         self.snapshot
270:             .get(node as usize)
271:             .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
272:             .and_then(|s| s.text.as_deref())
273:     }
274: 
275:     fn snapshot_property(&self, node: u32, prop: u16) -> Option<u32> {
276:         self.snapshot
277:             .get(node as usize)
278:             .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
279:             .and_then(|s| s.properties.get(&prop).copied())
280:     }
281: 
282:     fn slot_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Option<SnapshotNode> {
283:         let idx = id as usize;
284:         if self.snapshot.len() <= idx {
285:             self.snapshot.resize(idx + 1, None);
286:         }
287:         &mut self.snapshot[idx]
288:     }
289: 
290:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
291:     fn reconcile_node(
292:         &mut self,
293:         node: &Node,
294:         parent: Option<u32>,
295:         index: usize,
296:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
297:         out: &mut usize,
298:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
299:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
300: 
301:         // Resolve bindings (owned) before taking the mutable snapshot borrow.
302:         let bound_text: Option<String> = node
303:             .text_binding
304:             .and_then(|sid| self.store.get(sid))
305:             .and_then(SignalValue::to_text)
306:             .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
307: 
308:         let merged_props: Option<BTreeMap<u16, u32>> = if node.property_bindings.is_empty() {
309:             None
310:         } else {
311:             let mut m = node.properties.clone();
312:             for (prop, sid) in &node.property_bindings {
313:                 if let Some(v) = self.store.get(*sid).and_then(SignalValue::to_property_u32) {
314:                     m.insert(*prop, v);
315:                 }
316:             }
317:             Some(m)
318:         };
319: 
320:         let text_borrowed: Option<&str> = match (&bound_text, &node.component) {
321:             (Some(s), _) => Some(s.as_str()),
322:             (None, Component::Text { text }) => Some(text.as_str()),
323:             (None, Component::Button { label }) => Some(label.as_str()),
324:             _ => None,
325:         };
326:         let props: &BTreeMap<u16, u32> = merged_props.as_ref().unwrap_or(&node.properties);
327:         let token_refs = &node.token_properties;
328: 
329:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
330:         let token_changed = match &prev {
331:             Some(p) => p.token_refs.len() != token_refs.len()
332:                 || p.token_refs
333:                     .iter()
334:                     .any(|(prop, (old, _))| token_refs.get(prop) != Some(old)),
335:             None => !token_refs.is_empty(),
336:         };
337:         let props_changed = match &prev {
338:             Some(p) => &p.properties != props || token_changed,
339:             None => !props.is_empty() || !token_refs.is_empty(),
340:         };
341:         let text_changed = match &prev {
342:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
343:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
344:         };
345: 
346:         // Token-ref emission. Built only on mount or when a ref changed, so a
347:         // steady-state pass performs no heap allocations (the unchanged refs'
348:         // arena offsets are reused from the previous snapshot below).
349:         let mut token_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>> = None;
350: 
351:         // Properties in two passes — literals (skipping token-ref'd ids) then
352:         // token refs — so the steady-state emit performs no heap allocations.
353:         match &prev {
354:             None => {
355:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
356:                 *out += 1;
357:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
358:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
359:                     *out += 1;
360:                 }
361:                 for (prop, value) in props {
362:                     if token_refs.contains_key(prop) {
363:                         continue;
364:                     }
365:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
366:                     *out += 1;
367:                 }
368:                 if !token_refs.is_empty() {
369:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
370:                     for (prop, path) in token_refs {
371:                         let arena = guest
372:                             .alloc_str(path)
373:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
374:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN, arena)?;
375:                         *out += 1;
376:                         m.insert(*prop, (path.clone(), arena));
377:                     }
378:                     token_emit = Some(m);
379:                 }
380:                 if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
381:                     guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
382:                     *out += 1;
383:                 }
384:             }
385:             Some(p) => {
386:                 if p.parent != parent {
387:                     if let Some(old) = p.parent {
388:                         guest.remove_child(old, node.id)?;
389:                         *out += 1;
390:                     }
391:                     if let Some(new) = parent {
392:                         guest.insert_child(new, node.id, index as u32)?;
393:                         *out += 1;
394:                     }
395:                 } else if p.index != index {
396:                     if let Some(par) = parent {
397:                         guest.move_child(par, node.id, index as u32)?;
398:                         *out += 1;
399:                     }
400:                 }
401:                 if p.component_type != component_type {
402:                     guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
403:                     *out += 1;
404:                 }
405:                 if text_changed {
406:                     if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
407:                         guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
408:                         *out += 1;
409:                     }
410:                 }
411:                 for (prop, value) in props {
412:                     if token_refs.contains_key(prop) {
413:                         continue;
414:                     }
415:                     if p.properties.get(prop) != Some(value) {
416:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
417:                         *out += 1;
418:                     }
419:                 }
420:                 if token_changed {
421:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
422:                     for (prop, path) in token_refs {
423:                         let (arena, changed) = match p.token_refs.get(prop) {
424:                             Some((old_path, old_offset)) if old_path == path => (*old_offset, false),
425:                             _ => {
426:                                 let offset = guest
427:                                     .alloc_str(path)
428:                                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
429:                                 (offset, true)
430:                             }
431:                         };
432:                         m.insert(*prop, (path.clone(), arena));
433:                         if changed {
434:                             guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN, arena)?;
435:                             *out += 1;
436:                         }
437:                     }
438:                     token_emit = Some(m);
439:                 }
440:             }
441:         }
442: 
443:         let mut prev_props = None;
444:         let mut prev_text = None;
445:         let mut prev_token_refs = None;
446:         if let Some(p) = prev {
447:             if !props_changed {
448:                 prev_props = Some(p.properties);
449:             }
450:             if !text_changed {
451:                 prev_text = p.text;
452:             }
453:             if !token_changed {
454:                 prev_token_refs = Some(p.token_refs);
455:             }
456:             let _ = p;
457:         }
458:         let properties = match prev_props {
459:             Some(props) => props,
460:             None => props.clone(),
461:         };
462:         let text = match prev_text {
463:             Some(t) => Some(t),
464:             None => text_borrowed.map(|s| s.to_owned()),
465:         };
466:         let token_refs_snapshot = match token_emit {
467:             Some(m) => m,
468:             None => prev_token_refs.unwrap_or_default(),
469:         };
470:         *self.slot_mut(node.id) = Some(SnapshotNode {
471:             component_type,
472:             parent,
473:             index,
474:             text,
475:             properties,
476:             token_refs: token_refs_snapshot,
477:             gen: self.gen,
478:         });
479: 
480:         // Record signal dependencies for this node.
481:         if let Some(sid) = node.text_binding {
482:             self.store.add_dep(sid, Dep::Text { node: node.id });
483:         }
484:         for (prop, sid) in &node.property_bindings {
485:             self.store.add_dep(*sid, Dep::Property { node: node.id, prop: *prop });
486:         }
487: 
488:         for (i, child) in node.children.iter().enumerate() {
489:             self.reconcile_node(child, Some(node.id), i, guest, out)?;
490:         }
491:         Ok(())
492:     }
493: }

1: //! Global design-token theme overrides (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`).
2: //!
3: //! A [`Theme`] is a batch of **global, renderer-wide token overrides** for a
4: //! single scheme — every builder defines **one value** (spec/TOKENS.md). An
5: //! [`AdaptiveTheme`] composes a light + dark [`Theme`] pair; the dark one is
6: //! emitted with the `dark.` scheme prefix. Themes are emitted once at mount via
7: //! [`Engine::apply_theme`](crate::Engine::apply_theme) /
8: //! [`Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`](crate::Engine::apply_adaptive_theme);
9: //! overrides are renderer state, so they **never re-emit nodes** and never
10: //! participate in the diff.
11: 
12: use alloc::string::{String, ToString};
13: use alloc::vec::Vec;
14: 
15: use pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue;
16: 
17: /// A batch of global design-token overrides for a single scheme (light/base).
18: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
19: pub struct Theme {
20:     overrides: Vec<(String, TokenValue)>,
21: }
22: 
23: impl Theme {
24:     /// An empty theme.
25:     pub fn new() -> Self {
26:         Self::default()
27:     }
28: 
29:     /// Override a token with a packed sRGB `0xAARRGGBB` color.
30:     pub fn color(mut self, path: &str, argb: u32) -> Self {
31:         self.push(path, TokenValue::Color(argb));
32:         self
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Override a token with an `F32` value (lengths are in device pixels).
36:     pub fn f32(mut self, path: &str, value: f32) -> Self {
37:         self.push(path, TokenValue::F32(value));
38:         self
39:     }
40: 
41:     /// Override a token with a `U32` value.
42:     pub fn u32(mut self, path: &str, value: u32) -> Self {
43:         self.push(path, TokenValue::U32(value));
44:         self
45:     }
46: 
47:     /// Override a token with a `U8` value.
48:     pub fn u8(mut self, path: &str, value: u8) -> Self {
49:         self.push(path, TokenValue::U8(value));
50:         self
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Override a token with a `STRING` value (e.g. `font.body.family`). Rides
54:     /// the arena as a `STRING`-valued override.
55:     pub fn string(mut self, path: &str, value: &str) -> Self {
56:         self.push(path, TokenValue::Str(value.to_string()));
57:         self
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// Append a raw override with an explicit full path.
61:     pub fn override_token(mut self, path: &str, value: TokenValue) -> Self {
62:         self.overrides.push((path.to_string(), value));
63:         self
64:     }
65: 
66:     fn push(&mut self, path: &str, value: TokenValue) {
67:         self.overrides.push((path.to_string(), value));
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// The accumulated overrides (path, value) in insertion order.
71:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &TokenValue)> {
72:         self.overrides.iter().map(|(p, v)| (p.as_str(), v))
73:     }
74: }

2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface is the flat `builder`/`engine` world over a native shared-memory
13: //! transport.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::{Engine, SignalId, SignalValue};
18: use pathland_core::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_core_transport::{
20:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
21: };
22: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};
23: 
24: mod capi;
25: 
26: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct FlatNode {
29:     pub id: u32,
30:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
31:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
32:     /// A signal the node's text is bound to (overrides the component text).
33:     pub text_binding: Option<SignalId>,
34:     /// Property signals (propertyId → signal), overriding static properties.
35:     pub property_bindings: BTreeMap<u16, SignalId>,
36:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
37:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
38: }

40: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
41: /// zero-copy ring.

43:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
44:     engine: Engine,
45:     ring: RingTransport,
46: }

53: }

55: impl NativeHost {
56:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
57:     pub fn new() -> Self {
58:         Self {
59:             nodes: HashMap::new(),

74:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
75:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
76:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
77:             id,
78:             view_component: component.clone(),
79:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
80:             text_binding: None,
81:             property_bindings: BTreeMap::new(),
82:             parent: None,
83:             children: Vec::new(),
84:         });
85:         entry.view_component = component;
86:         entry.properties.clear();
87:         entry.text_binding = None;
88:         entry.property_bindings.clear();
89:     }

91:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
92:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
93:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
94:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
95:                 p.children.len()
96:             } else {
97:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
98:             };
99:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
100:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:             }
102:         }
103:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
104:             c.parent = Some(parent);
105:         }
106:     }
