108:     /// Remove `child` from `parent`.
109:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) {
110:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
111:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
112:         }
113:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
114:             c.parent = None;
115:         }

177:     pub fn set_signal(&mut self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> bool {
178:         let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
179:         guest.begin_frame();
180:         let n = self.engine.set_signal(id, value, &mut guest).unwrap_or(0);
181:         guest.end_frame();

185:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
186:     ///
187:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
188:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
189:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
190:         if let Some(root) = root {
191:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
192:             guest.begin_frame();
193:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
194:             guest.end_frame();
195:             true
196:         } else {
197:             false
198:         }
199:     }

201:     /// The ring's linear-memory buffer (for embedding / FFI).
202:     pub fn ring_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
203:         self.ring.buffer()
204:     }

208:         self.ring

212:     pub fn layout(&self) -> MemoryLayout {
213:         *self.layout_ref()
214:     }

217:         self.ring.layout()
218:     }

221:     pub fn root_id(&self) -> Option<u32> {
222:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none()).map(|n| n.id)
223:     }

225:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
226:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
227:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
228:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
229:         node.id = flat.id;
230:         node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
231:         node.text_binding = flat.text_binding;
232:         node.property_bindings = flat.property_bindings.clone();
233:         for child_id in &flat.children {
234:             if let Some(child) = self.materialize(*child_id) {
235:                 node.children.push(child);
236:             }
237:         }
238:         Some(node)
239:     }

1: //! Shared-memory ring transport (zero-copy, SPSC).
2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_core::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_core::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is
7: //! the high-performance local path.
8: 
9: use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout};
10: 
11: use crate::traits::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};
12: 
13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }
25: 
26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Create a ring transport over a caller-provided buffer/layout.
36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /// The memory layout (region geometry).
41:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
42:         &self.layout
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Create a producer view over the shared buffer (writes opcodes + arena).
46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Peak at the raw underlying buffer (for embedding/custom transports).
54:     pub fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
55:         &self.mem
56:     }
57: }
58: 
59: impl Default for RingTransport {
60:     fn default() -> Self {
61:         Self::new()
62:     }
63: }
64: 
65: impl FrameSource for RingTransport {
66:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
67:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
68:         let mut frames = host.frames();
69:         match frames.pop() {
70:             Some(frame) => Ok(Some(OpcodeBatch::new(
71:                 frame,
72:                 crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
73:             ))),
74:             None => Ok(None),
75:         }
76:     }
77: }
78: 
79: impl DriverTransport for RingTransport {
80:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
81:         // The host writes the raw input as an EVENT-category opcode into the
82:         // host → guest event ring; the guest drains it via `drain_events`.
83:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
84:         host.send_event(event).map_err(|_| {
85:             TransportError::Protocol(crate::ProtocolError::BadInput)
86:         })
87:     }
88: }

91:     /// Drain raw-input events written by the host into the host → guest event
92:     /// ring, decoding each `EVENT` opcode (guest side).
93:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<pathland_core::Event> {
94:         let mut guest = self.producer();
95:         guest.drain_events()
96:     }
97: }

177:     #[test]
178:     fn next_frame_is_zero_copy() {
179:         // The ring is a single shared linear-memory buffer. Reading a frame
180:         // must borrow that buffer in place — never copy the opcode stream.
181:         // Prove two things:
182:         //  1. Reading N opcodes allocates O(1) bookkeeping, not O(N) storage
183:         //     (a copy of the opcode stream would allocate per-opcode).
184:         //  2. The arena string decoded from the frame lives inside the shared
185:         //     buffer (pointer identity), i.e. it is read in place.
186: 
187:         use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout as AllocLayout};
188:         use std::cell::Cell;
189:         use std::thread_local;
190: 
191:         thread_local! {
192:             static COUNT: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };
193:         }
194:         struct Counting;
195:         unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Counting {
196:             unsafe fn alloc(&self, l: AllocLayout) -> *mut u8 {
197:                 COUNT.with(|c| c.set(c.get() + 1));
198:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
199:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.alloc(l) }
200:             }
201:             unsafe fn dealloc(&self, p: *mut u8, l: AllocLayout) {
202:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
203:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.dealloc(p, l) }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         #[global_allocator]
207:         static A: Counting = Counting;
208: 
209:         const OPCODES: usize = 1000;
210: 
211:         let mut ring = RingTransport::new();
212:         let buf_base = ring.buffer().as_ptr() as usize;
213:         let buf_end = buf_base + ring.buffer().len();
214: 
215:         // Producer writes opcodes + a string into the shared buffer (no copies).
216:         let arena_ref = {
217:             let mut guest = ring.producer();
218:             guest.begin_frame();
219:             for i in 0..OPCODES {
220:                 guest.create_node(i as u32 + 1, 0x0001).unwrap();
221:             }
222:             let r = guest.set_text(1, "zero-copy proof").unwrap();
223:             guest.end_frame();
224:             r
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Consumer reads the frame. Count allocations: the opcode stream is
228:         // borrowed, so allocations must be O(1), independent of the opcode count.
229:         COUNT.with(|c| c.set(0));
230:         let batch = ring.next_frame().unwrap().expect("a frame");
231:         let frame = batch.frame();
232: 
233:         let decoded: usize = frame.opcodes().count();
234:         let arena = frame.arena_str(arena_ref).expect("arena string");
235: 
236:         let allocs = COUNT.with(|c| c.get());
237: 
238:         assert_eq!(decoded, OPCODES + 1, "create_node + set_text");
239:         assert_eq!(arena, "zero-copy proof");
240: 
241:         // The arena string is read in place from the shared buffer.
242:         let str_ptr = arena.as_ptr() as usize;
243:         assert!(
244:             str_ptr >= buf_base && str_ptr < buf_end,
245:             "arena string must be borrowed from the shared ring (ptr {str_ptr:#x} outside {buf_base:#x}..{buf_end:#x})"
246:         );
247: 
248:         // No per-opcode copying: a handful of O(1) bookkeeping allocations is
249:         // fine; anything O(opcodes) would mean the opcode stream was copied.
250:         assert!(
251:             allocs < OPCODES,
252:             "reading {OPCODES} opcodes must not copy them (allocations: {allocs})"
253:         );
254:     }
255: }

1: //! # pathland-core-transport
2: //!
3: //! How Pathland opcodes are transported from the guest engine to host
4: //! renderers. There are two peer backends:
5: //!
6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native/WASM): the ring buffer + arena in
7: //!   `pathland-core` (`Guest`/`Host`). Zero-copy. This crate treats it as
8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.
9: //! - **Network batch** (SSR → browser): opcodes + string data serialized into
10: //!   **batches**.
11: //!
12: //! There are two network codecs, for two different relationships between the
13: //! producer and the consumer:
14: //!
15: //! - **Self-contained frames** ([`encode_frame`] / [`decode_frame`]) — each
16: //!   batch carries its own string section and `SET_TEXT` references strings by
17: //!   a *relative* offset into that section. The consumer needs **no prior
18: //!   state**: every message is independent. This is the streaming codec used
19: //!   for live deltas over WebSocket.
20: //! - **Arena-delta batches** ([`encode_batch`] / [`BatchEncoder`] /
21: //!   [`BatchDecoder`]) — the batch carries only the bytes *appended* to the
22: //!   arena since the previous batch, and `SET_TEXT` references absolute arena
23: //!   offsets. The consumer mirrors the arena so those offsets stay valid. This
24: //!   mirrors the shared-memory arena over a wire and is the ring-compatible
25: //!   codec (kept for a future WASM/embedded guest).
26: //!
27: //! ## Batch wire format (both codecs share the header)
28: //!
29: //! ```text
30: //! magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
31: //! | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | stringsLen (u32)
32: //! | string bytes (length-prefixed entries: [u32 len][bytes])
33: //! ```
34: //!
35: //! For a self-contained frame the trailing section is that frame's own string
36: //! table; for an arena-delta batch it is the arena bytes appended since the
37: //! last batch.
38: //!
39: //! ## Example (producer)
40: //!
41: //! ```no_run
42: //! use pathland_core_transport::{Batcher, BatchPolicy, BatchEncoder};
43: //! use std::time::Duration;
44: //!
45: //! let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_millis(4), 1400);
46: //! let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
47: //! let mut encoder = BatchEncoder::new();
48: //!
49: //! // batcher.push_frame(&frame) accumulates opcodes + arena delta;
50: //! // batcher.flush() -> Option<Vec<u8>> produces the serialized batch.
51: //! ```

1: //! Transport abstraction: how opcode batches move from producer to consumer.
2: //!
3: //! The UI runtime produces renderer-neutral opcodes and knows nothing about the
4: //! transport. This module defines the boundary between:
5: //!
6: //! - the **producer** (opcode engine) that emits opcodes, and
7: //! - the **consumer** (driver) that reads them.
8: //!
9: //! Local transports (shared-memory ring) may be zero-copy; remote transports
10: //! (WebSocket/IPC) copy and serialize. Both conform to the same traits.
11: //!
12: //! The two ends are deliberately separate because a transport is often split
13: //! across a process/IPC boundary, with different backpressure and blocking
14: //! semantics on each side.
15: 
16: use pathland_core::Frame;
17: 
18: /// A single in-memory transport unit: one frame of opcodes + arena plus
19: /// transport metadata. Distinct from the raw opcode stream and from the
20: /// wire-format batch.
21: pub struct OpcodeBatch<'a> {
22:     frame: Frame<'a>,
23:     /// Transport direction bitmask (see [`crate::direction`]).
24:     direction: u16,
25: }
26: 
27: impl<'a> OpcodeBatch<'a> {
28:     /// Wrap a frame as a transport batch (guest → host by default).
29:     pub fn new(frame: Frame<'a>, direction: u16) -> Self {
30:         Self { frame, direction }
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// The frame carried by this batch.
34:     pub fn frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
35:         &self.frame
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Transport direction bitmask.
39:     pub fn direction(&self) -> u16 {
40:         self.direction
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: /// Errors produced by a transport while sending or receiving.
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub enum TransportError {
47:     /// The consumer has not drained; the producer should retain and retry.
48:     Backpressure,
49:     /// The transport is closed/terminated.
50:     Closed,
51:     /// The peer violated the protocol.
52:     Protocol(ProtocolError),
53: }
54: 
55: /// Sub-errors for protocol violations.
56: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
57: pub enum ProtocolError {
58:     /// The remote sent a version this side does not support.
59:     BadVersion,
60:     /// The payload is malformed (bad magic, truncated, bad length).
61:     Malformed,
62:     /// A raw input could not be interpreted.
63:     BadInput,
64: }
65: 
66: /// Handles raw-input events arriving from the host (renderer → engine).
67: ///
68: /// The driver resolves a raw input to a node id (via hit-testing) and dispatches
69: /// it here; the transport's guest side forwards it to the guest engine.
70: pub trait InputSink {
71:     /// Deliver a raw input (host → guest).
72:     fn dispatch(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event);
73: }
74: 
75: /// The consumer side of a transport: the driver reads frames here.
76: ///
77: /// A transport may be blocking or non-blocking; `next_frame` reflects that.
78: /// The returned `Frame` borrows the transport's backing memory (zero-copy when
79: /// possible); consume it before the next call.
80: pub trait FrameSource {
81:     /// Read the next available frame, or `None` if none is ready.
82:     ///
83:     /// Blocking vs non-blocking semantics are transport-specific (documented
84:     /// per implementation).
85:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
86: }
87: 
88: /// A consumer-side transport that can also send raw inputs back to the guest.
89: pub trait DriverTransport: FrameSource {
90:     /// Send a raw input from the host to the guest over this transport.
91:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
92: }

1: //! Batching policy and buffering for network transport.
2: //!
3: //! `Batcher` accumulates frames against a [`BatchPolicy`] and flushes a single
4: //! serialized batch when either the time interval since the first buffered
5: //! opcode elapses **or** the accumulated byte size reaches the threshold —
6: //! first trigger wins.
7: 
8: use alloc::vec::Vec;
9: use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
10: 
11: use pathland_core::Opcode;
12: 
13: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
14: use crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST;
15: 
16: /// Default time interval before a batch is flushed (4 ms).
17: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(4);
18: /// Default max batch byte size (conservative network frame / MTU).
19: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES: usize = 1400;
20: 
21: /// Flush thresholds for network batching.
22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
23: pub struct BatchPolicy {
24:     /// Flush when this much time has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
25:     pub max_interval: Duration,
26:     /// Flush when the accumulated batch reaches this many bytes.
27:     pub max_batch_bytes: usize,
28: }
29: 
30: impl BatchPolicy {
31:     /// Create a policy from a time interval and a max batch size.
32:     pub const fn new(max_interval: Duration, max_batch_bytes: usize) -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             max_interval,
35:             max_batch_bytes,
36:         }
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// The default policy: 4 ms interval, 1400-byte batches.
40:     pub const fn default_policy() -> Self {
41:         Self::new(DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL, DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES)
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl Default for BatchPolicy {
46:     fn default() -> Self {
47:         Self::default_policy()
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: /// Accumulates frames into a batch and flushes per [`BatchPolicy`].
52: ///
53: /// The arena is append-only; the batcher ships the bytes appended since the
54: /// last flush (tracked by arena length). If the arena shrank (a `META::RESET`),
55: /// the pending arena is reset so the next flush starts fresh.
56: #[derive(Debug)]
57: pub struct Batcher {
58:     policy: BatchPolicy,
59:     /// Frame count of the first buffered frame.
60:     frame_count: u32,
61:     /// Opcodes buffered since the last flush.
62:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
63:     /// Arena bytes appended since the last flush.
64:     pending_arena: Vec<u8>,
65:     /// Arena length at the last flush.
66:     last_arena_len: usize,
67:     /// When the first opcode of the current batch was buffered.
68:     started: Option<Instant>,
69:     /// Size trigger latched on push.
70:     size_triggered: bool,
71: }
72: 
73: impl Batcher {
74:     /// Create a batcher with the given policy.
75:     pub fn new(policy: BatchPolicy) -> Self {
76:         Self {
77:             policy,
78:             frame_count: 0,
79:             opcodes: Vec::new(),
80:             pending_arena: Vec::new(),
81:             last_arena_len: 0,
82:             started: None,
83:             size_triggered: false,
84:         }
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Create a batcher with the default policy (4 ms / 1400 B).
88:     pub fn default_policy() -> Self {
89:         Self::new(BatchPolicy::default())
90:     }
91: 
92:     /// Whether no opcodes are currently buffered.
93:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
94:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Number of opcodes buffered since the last flush (diagnostics).
98:     pub fn pending_opcodes(&self) -> usize {
99:         self.opcodes.len()
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// Approximate bytes that would be shipped on flush (diagnostics).
103:     pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
104:         self.opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + self.pending_arena.len() + crate::batch::BATCH_HEADER + 4
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Record a frame (opcodes + the arena's used portion `[0..cursor)`),
108:     /// accumulating the arena delta. Returns `true` if the size trigger fired.
109:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> bool {
110:         if self.started.is_none() {
111:             self.started = Some(Instant::now());
112:             self.frame_count = frame_count;
113:         }
114:         if arena_used.len() < self.last_arena_len {
115:             // Arena was reset; restart the pending buffer.
116:             self.pending_arena.clear();
117:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
118:         }
119:         self.pending_arena.extend_from_slice(&arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]);
120:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
121:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
122: 
123:         self.size_triggered |= self.pending_bytes() >= self.policy.max_batch_bytes;
124:         self.size_triggered
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Whether the time interval has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
128:     pub fn interval_elapsed(&self) -> bool {
129:         match self.started {
130:             Some(t) => t.elapsed() >= self.policy.max_interval,
131:             None => false,
132:         }
133:     }
134: 
135:     /// Serialize and reset the current buffer, returning the batch bytes.
136:     ///
137:     /// Flushes when `force` is true or either policy trigger fired. Returns
138:     /// `None` when nothing is buffered.
139:     pub fn flush(&mut self, force: bool) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
140:         if self.opcodes.is_empty() {
141:             return None;
142:         }
143:         let should_flush = force || self.size_triggered || self.interval_elapsed();
144:         if !should_flush {
145:             return None;
146:         }
147:         let bytes = encode_batch(
148:             self.frame_count,
149:             GUEST_TO_HOST,
150:             &self.opcodes,
151:             &self.pending_arena,
152:         );
153:         self.opcodes.clear();
154:         self.pending_arena.clear();
155:         self.last_arena_len = 0;
156:         self.started = None;
157:         self.size_triggered = false;
158:         Some(bytes)
159:     }
160: }

1: //! Batch wire format: encode/decode opcodes + arena delta into network batches.
2: 
3: use alloc::vec::Vec;
4: use pathland_core::{Event, Frame, Opcode, category, event, meta};
5: 
6: use crate::{BATCH_MAGIC, BATCH_VERSION};
7: 
8: /// Fixed header byte length: magic(4) + version(2) + flags(2) + frameCount(4) + opcodeCount(4).
9: pub const BATCH_HEADER: usize = 16;
10: 
11: /// Errors produced while decoding a network batch.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum BatchError {
14:     /// The batch is shorter than the fixed header.
15:     Truncated,
16:     /// The batch magic does not match `BATCH_MAGIC`.
17:     BadMagic,
18:     /// The batch version is not supported.
19:     BadVersion,
20:     /// The opcode payload is truncated (opcodeCount × 16 exceeds the buffer).
21:     BadOpcodeCount,
22:     /// The arena delta length exceeds the remaining buffer.
23:     BadArenaLen,
24: }
25: 
26: /// A decoded network batch: opcodes plus a mirrored arena, exposed as a
27: /// `pathland_core::Frame` so consumers (`RenderTree::apply_frame`) work
28: /// exactly as with shared-memory frames.
29: pub struct Batch<'a> {
30:     frame: Frame<'a>,
31:     frame_count: u32,
32:     flags: u16,
33: }
34: 
35: impl<'a> core::fmt::Debug for Batch<'a> {
36:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
37:         f.debug_struct("Batch")
38:             .field("frame_count", &self.frame_count)
39:             .field("flags", &self.flags)
40:             .field("len", &self.len())
41:             .finish()
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl<'a> Batch<'a> {
46:     /// The opcodes carried by this batch, in order.
47:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Opcode> + '_ {
48:         self.frame.opcodes()
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Number of opcodes in the batch.
52:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
53:         self.frame.len()
54:     }
55: 
56:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
57:         self.frame.is_empty()
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// The guest frame count the batch spans.
61:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
62:         self.frame_count
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Direction flags (see [`crate::direction`]).
66:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
67:         self.flags
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// View this batch as a `Frame` (the transport seam).
71:     pub fn as_frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
72:         &self.frame
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Frame::arena_get`).
76:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], pathland_core::ArenaError> {
77:         self.frame.arena_get(offset)
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
81:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, pathland_core::ArenaError> {
82:         self.frame.arena_str(offset)
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// Serialize one batch from opcodes + an arena delta (bytes appended since the
87: /// previous batch). Stateless; see [`BatchEncoder`] for cursor tracking.
88: pub fn encode_batch(
89:     frame_count: u32,
90:     flags: u16,
91:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
92:     arena_delta: &[u8],
93: ) -> Vec<u8> {
94:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(BATCH_HEADER + opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + arena_delta.len() + 4);
95:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
96:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
97:     out.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
98:     out.extend_from_slice(&frame_count.to_le_bytes());
99:     out.extend_from_slice(&(opcodes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
100:     for op in opcodes {
101:         out.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
102:     }
103:     out.extend_from_slice(&(arena_delta.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
104:     out.extend_from_slice(arena_delta);
105:     out
106: }
107: 
108: /// Fields parsed from a batch header + payload regions.
109: struct ParsedBatch<'a> {
110:     flags: u16,
111:     frame_count: u32,
112:     opcodes: &'a [u8],
113:     arena_delta: &'a [u8],
114: }
115: 
116: /// Parse a batch header, returning flags, frame count, opcode bytes and arena delta.
117: fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ParsedBatch<'_>, BatchError> {
118:     if bytes.len() < BATCH_HEADER {
119:         return Err(BatchError::Truncated);
120:     }
121:     let magic = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
122:     if magic != BATCH_MAGIC {
123:         return Err(BatchError::BadMagic);
124:     }
125:     let version = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..6].try_into().unwrap());
126:     if version != BATCH_VERSION {
127:         return Err(BatchError::BadVersion);
128:     }
129:     let flags = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[6..8].try_into().unwrap());
130:     let frame_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
131:     let opcode_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
132: 
133:     let opcodes_bytes = opcode_count
134:         .checked_mul(Opcode::SIZE)
135:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
136:     let opcodes_start = BATCH_HEADER;
137:     let opcodes_end = opcodes_start
138:         .checked_add(opcodes_bytes)
139:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
140:     if opcodes_end > bytes.len() {
141:         return Err(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount);
142:     }
143:     let arena_len_pos = opcodes_end;
144:     if arena_len_pos + 4 > bytes.len() {
145:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
146:     }
147:     let arena_len = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[arena_len_pos..arena_len_pos + 4].try_into().unwrap())
148:         as usize;
149:     let arena_start = arena_len_pos + 4;
150:     let arena_end = arena_start
151:         .checked_add(arena_len)
152:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadArenaLen)?;
153:     if arena_end > bytes.len() {
154:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
155:     }
156: 
157:     Ok(ParsedBatch {
158:         flags,
159:         frame_count,
160:         opcodes: &bytes[opcodes_start..opcodes_end],
161:         arena_delta: &bytes[arena_start..arena_end],
162:     })
163: }
164: 
165: /// A streamed network-batch encoder.
166: ///
167: /// Tracks the last arena length so successive batches carry only the bytes
168: /// appended to the bump arena since the previous batch. If the arena is reset
169: /// (shrank — see `META::RESET`), the full used arena is sent and tracking
170: /// restarts.
171: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
172: pub struct BatchEncoder {
173:     last_arena_len: usize,
174: }
175: 
176: impl BatchEncoder {
177:     /// Create a fresh encoder (no arena bytes sent yet).
178:     pub fn new() -> Self {
179:         Self { last_arena_len: 0 }
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Encode a frame's opcodes plus the arena bytes appended since the last
183:     /// call. `arena_used` is the arena region's used portion (`[0..cursor)`).
184:     ///
185:     /// If the frame contains `META::RESET`, arena tracking restarts (the arena
186:     /// cursor returns to 0) and the full used arena is sent.
187:     pub fn encode(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
188:         let reset = opcodes.iter().any(|op| {
189:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
190:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
191:         });
192:         if reset {
193:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
194:         }
195:         let delta = if arena_used.len() >= self.last_arena_len {
196:             &arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]
197:         } else {
198:             // Arena shrank unexpectedly: send the full used arena again.
199:             arena_used
200:         };
201:         let bytes = encode_batch(frame_count, crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST, opcodes, delta);
202:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
203:         bytes
204:     }

207:     pub fn arena_sent(&self) -> usize {
208:         self.last_arena_len
209:     }

212: /// A streamed network-batch decoder.
213: ///
214: /// Maintains a **mirrored arena**: each batch's arena delta is appended, so
215: /// absolute `arenaRef` offsets resolve exactly as in shared memory. When a
216: /// batch contains `META::RESET`, the mirror is cleared before appending.
217: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
218: pub struct BatchDecoder {
219:     arena: Vec<u8>,
220: }
221: 
222: impl BatchDecoder {
223:     /// Create an empty decoder.
224:     pub fn new() -> Self {
225:         Self { arena: Vec::new() }
226:     }
227: 
228:     /// Decode a batch, appending its arena delta to the mirror.
229:     ///
230:     /// The returned `Batch` borrows `bytes` (opcodes) and this decoder (arena);
231:     /// keep both alive while consuming it.
232:     pub fn decode<'a>(&'a mut self, bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Batch<'a>, BatchError> {
233:         let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
234: 
235:         // A META::RESET in the batch clears the renderer; reset the arena mirror
236:         // to match (offsets restart at 0 after a reset).
237:         let opcode_count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
238:         let reset = (0..opcode_count).any(|i| {
239:             let op = Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[i * Opcode::SIZE..(i + 1) * Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap());
240:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
241:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
242:         });
243:         if reset {
244:             self.arena.clear();
245:         }
246:         self.arena.extend_from_slice(parsed.arena_delta);
247: 
248:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(parsed.opcodes, &self.arena, 0, parsed.opcodes.len());
249:         Ok(Batch {
250:             frame,
251:             frame_count: parsed.frame_count,
252:             flags: parsed.flags,
253:         })
254:     }
255: 
256:     /// The mirrored arena length (diagnostics).
257:     pub fn arena_len(&self) -> usize {
258:         self.arena.len()
259:     }
260: }

262: /// Encode raw-input events as a host → guest batch.
263: ///
264: /// Events are `EVENT`-category opcodes; the batch reuses the wire format with
265: /// the `HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag. `TextChanged` events carry their text in
266: /// the batch's string section (a length-prefixed entry referenced by the
267: /// opcode's `B` offset), as do `Navigate` URLs; the string section is only
268: /// empty when there are no such events.
269: pub fn encode_events(frame_count: u32, events: &[Event]) -> Vec<u8> {
270:     let mut opcodes = Vec::new();
271:     let mut strings = Vec::new();
272:     for ev in events {
273:         match ev {
274:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
275:                 let offset = strings.len() as u32;
276:                 strings.extend_from_slice(&(value.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
277:                 strings.extend_from_slice(value.as_bytes());
278:                 opcodes.push(Opcode::new(
279:                     category::EVENT,
280:                     event::TEXT_CHANGED,
281:                     0,
282:                     *target,
283:                     offset,
284:                     0,
285:                 ));
286:             }
287:             Event::Navigate { url: Some(url) } => {
288:                 let offset = strings.len() as u32;
289:                 strings.extend_from_slice(&(url.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
290:                 strings.extend_from_slice(url.as_bytes());
291:                 opcodes.push(Opcode::new(
292:                     category::EVENT,
293:                     event::NAVIGATE,
294:                     pathland_core::flag::NAVIGATE_URL,
295:                     0,
296:                     offset,
297:                     0,
298:                 ));
299:             }
300:             other => opcodes.push(other.encode()),
301:         }
302:     }
303:     encode_batch(frame_count, crate::direction::HOST_TO_GUEST, &opcodes, &strings)
304: }

306: /// Decode a host → guest event batch, returning `(frame_count, events)`.
307: ///
308: /// Unknown or malformed event opcodes are skipped. `TextChanged` opcodes and
309: /// `Navigate` URL opcodes resolve their strings from the batch's string section.
310: pub fn decode_events(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(u32, Vec<Event>), BatchError> {
311:     let mut decoder = BatchDecoder::new();
312:     let batch = decoder.decode(bytes)?;
313:     let events = batch
314:         .opcodes()
315:         .filter_map(|op| {
316:             if op.category() == category::EVENT && op.command() == event::TEXT_CHANGED {
317:                 batch
318:                     .arena_str(op.b())
319:                     .ok()
320:                     .map(|text| Event::TextChanged {
321:                         target: op.a(),
322:                         value: text.to_string(),
323:                     })
324:             } else if op.category() == category::EVENT && op.command() == event::NAVIGATE {
325:                 if op.flags() & pathland_core::flag::NAVIGATE_URL != 0 {
326:                     batch
327:                         .arena_str(op.b())
328:                         .ok()
329:                         .map(|url| Event::Navigate {
330:                             url: Some(url.to_string()),
331:                         })
332:                 } else {
333:                     Some(Event::Navigate { url: None })
334:                 }
335:             } else {
336:                 Event::try_from(op).ok()
337:             }
338:         })
339:         .collect();
340:     Ok((batch.frame_count(), events))
341: }
342: 
343: /// Build a self-contained `Frame` view over in-memory opcodes + a string
344: /// section — the **in-process transport seam**.
345: ///
346: /// `slots` is reused as the opcode byte buffer (cleared, then the 16-byte
347: /// opcodes written in), so the returned `Frame` borrows both `slots` and
348: /// `strings` with no serialization. This is how an in-process consumer receives
349: /// the same `Frame` view a ring or network decoder would produce.
350: pub fn frame_from_slices<'a>(
351:     slots: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
352:     strings: &'a [u8],
353:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
354: ) -> Frame<'a> {
355:     slots.clear();
356:     slots.extend(opcodes.iter().flat_map(Opcode::to_bytes));
357:     let bytes: &'a [u8] = slots;
358:     Frame::from_parts(bytes, strings, 0, bytes.len())
359: }
360: 
361: /// Encode a **self-contained** frame as a network batch.
362: ///
363: /// `opcodes` is the frame's commands and `strings` its per-frame string
364: /// section: every `SET_TEXT` opcode references its string by a *relative*
365: /// offset into `strings` (not an absolute arena offset). The batch therefore
366: /// decodes with no prior state — no mirrored arena, no delta tracking — which
367: /// is what makes each WebSocket message independent.
368: ///
369: /// This is the network/stream codec. The shared-memory path uses
370: /// [`encode_batch`]/[`BatchEncoder`] instead, whose arena offsets are absolute
371: /// and mirrored on the consumer.
372: pub fn encode_frame(opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
373:     encode_batch(0, crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST, opcodes, strings)
374: }
375: 
376: /// Encode a `META::RESYNC` request batch (host → guest): the host (renderer)
377: /// asks the guest (application) to re-send the full tree as a snapshot.
378: /// `A/B/C` are all zero; the guest answers with a full-snapshot batch.
379: pub fn encode_resync() -> Vec<u8> {
380:     encode_batch(
381:         0,
382:         crate::direction::HOST_TO_GUEST,
383:         &[Opcode::new(category::META, meta::RESYNC, 0, 0, 0, 0)],
384:         &[],
385:     )
386: }
387: 
388: /// Decode a self-contained frame batch, returning `(opcodes, strings)`.
389: ///
390: /// Stateless: unlike [`BatchDecoder`], no arena mirror is maintained, because
391: /// the batch carries its own string section and the offsets are relative to it.
392: pub fn decode_frame(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Vec<Opcode>, Vec<u8>), BatchError> {
393:     let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
394:     let count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
395:     let opcodes = (0..count)
396:         .map(|i| {
397:             let start = i * Opcode::SIZE;
398:             Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[start..start + Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap())
399:         })
400:         .collect();
401:     Ok((opcodes, parsed.arena_delta.to_vec()))
402: }

1: //! Network batch transport (remote path).
2: //!
3: //! Producer side serializes Frames into network batches (opcodes + arena delta);
4: //! the consumer decodes them with `BatchDecoder` (see `crate::batch`) back into
5: //! `Frame` views consumed by `RenderTree::apply_frame`. This is the remote/SSR
6: //! path where producer and consumer do **not** share memory.
7: //!
8: //! The wire format is unchanged from `crate::batch` (magic/version/flags/
9: //! frameCount/opcodeCount/opcodes/arenaDeltaLen/arena).
10: 
11: use alloc::vec::Vec;
12: 
13: use pathland_core::{Frame, Opcode};
14: 
15: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
16: 
17: /// Producer-side network batch encoder.
18: ///
19: /// Buffers opcodes (from Frames) and serializes them into a batch with the
20: /// arena's used-arena slice. Use the `Batcher` helper (`crate::batching`) for a
21: /// time/size flush policy; this type is the bare encoder for explicit flushes.
22: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
23: pub struct NetBatchEncoder {
24:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
25: }
26: 
27: impl NetBatchEncoder {
28:     /// Append a frame's opcodes to the pending batch.
29:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
30:         self.opcodes.extend(frame.opcodes());
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// Append raw opcodes to the pending batch.
34:     pub fn push_opcodes(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode]) {
35:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Serialize the pending opcodes with a provided used-arena slice, clearing
39:     /// the buffer. `frame_count` is the covering frame counter.
40:     pub fn encode_with_arena(&mut self, frame_count: u32, arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
41:         let bytes = encode_batch(
42:             frame_count,
43:             crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
44:             &self.opcodes,
45:             arena_used,
46:         );
47:         self.opcodes.clear();
48:         bytes
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Whether any opcodes are buffered.
52:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
53:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
54:     }
55: 
56:     /// Number of buffered opcodes.
57:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
58:         self.opcodes.len()
59:     }
60: }

30: /// A resolved token value. Mirrors the wire value types; `Str` is the resolved
31: /// form of a `STRING`-valued token (the wire carries an arena ref instead).
32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
33: pub enum TokenValue {
34:     Color(u32),

36:     U32(u32),
37:     U8(u8),
38:     I32(i32),

42: impl TokenValue {
43:     /// The wire `value_type` for this value.
44:     pub fn value_type(&self) -> u8 {
45:         match self {
46:             TokenValue::Color(_) => crate::value_type::COLOR,
47:             TokenValue::F32(_) => crate::value_type::F32,
48:             TokenValue::U32(_) => crate::value_type::U32,
49:             TokenValue::U8(_) => crate::value_type::U8,
50:             TokenValue::I32(_) => crate::value_type::I32,
51:             TokenValue::Str(_) => crate::value_type::STRING,
52:         }
53:     }
54: 
55:     /// Decode a wire `(value_type, value)` into a token value. `STRING` returns
56:     /// `None` — the wire carries an arena ref there; resolve it and build
57:     /// [`TokenValue::Str`] directly.
58:     pub fn from_wire(value_type: u8, value: u32) -> Option<Self> {
59:         match value_type {
60:             crate::value_type::COLOR => Some(TokenValue::Color(value)),
61:             crate::value_type::F32 => Some(TokenValue::F32(f32::from_bits(value))),
62:             crate::value_type::U32 => Some(TokenValue::U32(value)),
63:             crate::value_type::U8 => Some(TokenValue::U8((value & 0xFF) as u8)),
64:             crate::value_type::I32 => Some(TokenValue::I32(value as i32)),
65:             _ => None,
66:         }
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// The value as an `F32`, if this token is numeric.
70:     pub fn as_f32(&self) -> Option<f32> {
71:         match self {
72:             TokenValue::F32(v) => Some(*v),
73:             TokenValue::U32(v) => Some(*v as f32),
74:             TokenValue::U8(v) => Some(f32::from(*v)),
75:             TokenValue::I32(v) => Some(*v as f32),
76:             _ => None,
77:         }
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// The packed wire value (`C` field) for non-string values. `Str` returns
81:     /// `None` — the wire carries an arena ref there.
82:     pub fn to_bits(&self) -> Option<u32> {
83:         match self {
84:             TokenValue::Color(v) => Some(*v),
85:             TokenValue::F32(v) => Some(v.to_bits()),
86:             TokenValue::U32(v) => Some(*v),
87:             TokenValue::U8(v) => Some(u32::from(*v)),
88:             TokenValue::I32(v) => Some(*v as u32),
89:             TokenValue::Str(_) => None,
90:         }
91:     }
92: }

94: /// The four lookup tables a renderer consults, in resolution order:
95: /// app overrides (base + `dark.*`) and renderer defaults (base + `dark.*`).
96: ///
97: /// Overrides and defaults are keyed by **full path** in the base maps and by
98: /// **bare path** (the `dark.` prefix stripped) in the `dark` maps.
99: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
100: pub struct TokenTables<'a> {
101:     pub overrides: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
102:     pub dark_overrides: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
103:     pub defaults: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
104:     pub dark_defaults: &'a BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
105: }
106: 
107: /// Resolve a token path against the given tables and scheme.
108: ///
109: /// Resolution (spec/TOKENS.md):
110: /// 1. The **generative `space.<N>` family** resolves `space.base` (scheme-aware,
111: ///    with the same fallback chain) and multiplies by the numeric leaf.
112: /// 2. Walk the candidate chain — for the dark scheme, `dark.<path>` ancestors
113: ///    first, then the base ancestors; for light, base ancestors only.
114: /// 3. The first **app override** in the chain wins; otherwise the first
115: ///    **renderer default**; otherwise `None` (the renderer falls back).
116: pub fn resolve(
117:     path: &str,
118:     scheme: Scheme,
119:     tables: &TokenTables<'_>,
120: ) -> Option<TokenValue> {
121:     // Generative spacing family: `space.<N>` = `space.base` × N.
122:     if let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix("space.") {
123:         if let Ok(n) = rest.parse::<f32>() {
124:             if let Some(base) = resolve("space.base", scheme, tables) {
125:                 if let Some(base) = base.as_f32() {
126:                     return Some(TokenValue::F32(base * n));
127:                 }
128:             }
129:         }
130:     }
131: 
132:     let chain = parent_chain(path);
133: 
134:     // Override pass: the `dark.*` layer first (when the scheme is dark), then
135:     // the base layer — each consulted against its own override table.
136:     if scheme == Scheme::Dark {
137:         for &cand in &chain {
138:             if let Some(v) = tables.dark_overrides.get(cand) {
139:                 return Some(v.clone());
140:             }
141:         }
142:     }
143:     for &cand in &chain {
144:         if let Some(v) = tables.overrides.get(cand) {
145:             return Some(v.clone());
146:         }
147:     }
148: 
149:     // Default pass: same layer order against the renderer defaults.
150:     if scheme == Scheme::Dark {
151:         for &cand in &chain {
152:             if let Some(v) = tables.dark_defaults.get(cand) {
153:                 return Some(v.clone());
154:             }
155:         }
156:     }
157:     for &cand in &chain {
158:         if let Some(v) = tables.defaults.get(cand) {
159:             return Some(v.clone());
160:         }
161:     }
162:     None
163: }

165: /// The parent-fallback chain for a path: `font.body.size` →
166: /// `["font.body.size", "font.body", "font", ""]`.
167: fn parent_chain(path: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
168:     let mut chain = Vec::new();
169:     chain.push(path);
170:     let mut cur = path;
171:     while let Some(idx) = cur.rfind('.') {
172:         cur = &cur[..idx];
173:         chain.push(cur);
174:     }
175:     chain.push("");
176:     chain
177: }

1: //! # pathland-render-gtk
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **GTK4 renderer**. It consumes opcode frames (via
4: //! [`crate::host::RenderTree`]) and maps them **incrementally** onto native GTK4
5: //! widgets — `GtkBox` for stacks, `GtkLabel` for text, `GtkButton` for buttons.
6: //!
7: //! This is the only place in the desktop path that touches GTK/glib/pango APIs.
8: //! Demos author their UI with the Pathland DSL and drive this renderer; they
9: //! never call GTK directly.
10: //!
11: //! ## Rust host
12: //!
13: //! `GtkRenderer::run(app_id, title, ring, on_event)` owns the `gtk::Application`
14: //! / `ApplicationWindow` / main loop, pumps the shared ring (frames in, events
15: //! out), and dispatches raw-input [`Event`]s back to the application.
16: //!
17: //! ## Java host

19: //! The `pathland_gtk_*` C ABI (`capi` module) exposes the same renderer to a
20: //! foreign host (Java via JNA): `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)` runs GTK
21: //! in-process over the `pathland-view-native` host's shared ring.

49: /// The bidirectional transport surface the renderer pumps: frames in
50: /// (guest → host) and events out (host → guest).
51: ///
52: /// The renderer **never drains events** — it only writes them as `EVENT`
53: /// opcodes. The host (application) drains the event ring itself, so raw inputs
54: /// return to the app through the opcode engine, symmetric with how frames flow
55: /// to the renderer.
56: pub trait Pump {
57:     /// Read the next guest → host frame.
58:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
59:     /// Write a host → guest raw input as an `EVENT` opcode.
60:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
61: }

63: impl Pump for RingTransport {
64:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
65:         FrameSource::next_frame(self)
66:     }
67:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
68:         DriverTransport::send_input(self, event)
69:     }

184:     /// Reconcile the GTK widget tree against the current `RenderTree`.
185:     fn sync(&mut self) {

187:         let live: std::collections::HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
188:         let stale: Vec<u32> = self
189:             .widgets
190:             .keys()
191:             .copied()
192:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
193:             .collect();
194:         for id in stale {
195:             self.widgets.remove(&id);
196:             self.attached_listeners.remove(&id);
197:             self.composite_boxes.remove(&id);
198:             self.nav_views.remove(&id);

208:         //    reconcile each stack's child list/order.
209:         if let Some(root_id) = self.tree.root().map(|n| n.id) {

214:     fn sync_node(&mut self, id: u32) {
215:         let Some(node) = self.tree.node(id).cloned() else {

223:         let node = self.tree.node(id).cloned().unwrap_or(node);

227:         let children = node.children.clone();
228:         for child in &children {

232:         // Containers: reconcile the native children (order/content/positions)

234:         if is_container(node.component_type) {
235:             self.sync_container(id, &children, &node);
236:         } else if is_composite(&node) {

543:             Some(player) if player.source == resolved => player,

53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

55: /// Create a ring host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
56: /// handle (non-null on success).

60:         ring: RingTransport::new(),
61:     });

66: #[no_mangle]

68:     if !handle.is_null() {
69:         // SAFETY: `handle` is the pointer returned by `pathland_core_create`.
70:         drop(Box::from_raw(handle as *mut CoreHost));

72: }

75: // Ring (guest → host)
76: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77: 
78: /// Push one raw 16-byte opcode into the shared ring at `writeCursor`, advancing
79: /// it. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the ring is full or `opcode` is null.
80: #[no_mangle]
81: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: CoreHandle, opcode: *const u8) -> u8 {
82:     let Some(op) = opcode_from_ptr(opcode) else {
83:         return 0;
84:     };
85:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
86:     u8::from(guest.push_opcode(op).is_ok())

89: /// Allocate `len` bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute arena
90: /// offset (a `u32` reference for `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT` / `STRING` property values).
91: /// Returns `u32::MAX` when the arena is full or `bytes` is null.
92: #[no_mangle]
93: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_arena_alloc(
94:     handle: CoreHandle,
95:     bytes: *const u8,
96:     len: u32,
97: ) -> u32 {
98:     if bytes.is_null() {
99:         return u32::MAX;
100:     }
101:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `bytes` points to ≥ `len` readable bytes.
102:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(bytes, len as usize) };
103:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
104:     guest.alloc(slice).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
105: }

107: /// Record the start of a frame (frame boundaries delimit a batch of opcodes).
108: #[no_mangle]
109: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_begin_frame(handle: CoreHandle) {
110:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
111:     guest.begin_frame();
112: }

114: /// End the current frame, publishing `frameCount`.
115: #[no_mangle]
116: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_end_frame(handle: CoreHandle) {
117:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
118:     guest.end_frame();
119: }

121: /// The monotonic frame counter published so far.
122: #[no_mangle]
123: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_frame_count(handle: CoreHandle) -> u32 {
124:     let guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
125:     guest.frame_count()
126: }

128: /// Pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena) for zero-copy
129: /// reads. Never null.
130: #[no_mangle]
131: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle: CoreHandle) -> *const u8 {
132:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().as_ptr()
133: }
134: 
135: /// Total byte length of the shared linear memory buffer.
136: #[no_mangle]
137: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_len(handle: CoreHandle) -> u64 {
138:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().len() as u64
139: }
140: 
141: /// Borrow the underlying shared ring for a same-process consumer (e.g. the GTK
142: /// renderer, which pumps it in place). Returns NULL for a null handle.
143: ///
144: /// The caller must not destroy the core handle until the consumer is done with
145: /// the ring. The pointer is only valid inside this process.
146: #[no_mangle]
147: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_mut(handle: CoreHandle) -> *mut RingTransport {
148:     if handle.is_null() {
149:         return std::ptr::null_mut();
150:     }
151:     &mut as_host(handle).ring
152: }
153: 
154: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
155: // Events (host → guest)
156: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157: 
158: /// Drain pending raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
159: /// copying each 16-byte opcode into `out`. Returns the number of events
160: /// written (≤ `max`). `out` must point to ≥ `max * 16` writable bytes.
161: #[no_mangle]
162: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_drain_events(
163:     handle: CoreHandle,
164:     out: *mut u8,
165:     max: u32,
166: ) -> u32 {
167:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
168:         return 0;
169:     }
170:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
171:     let events = guest.drain_event_opcodes();
172:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
173:     for (i, op) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
174:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();
175:         // SAFETY: `out` points to ≥ max*16 writable bytes; we write ≤ max slots.
176:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
177:     }
178:     n as u32
179: }
180: 
181: /// Push one raw 16-byte `EVENT`-category opcode into the host → guest event
182: /// ring (the renderer reporting an input). Returns 1 on success.
183: #[no_mangle]

186:         return 0;
187:     };
188:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
189:     u8::from(guest.push_event_opcode(op).is_ok())
190: }

## 1. `pathland-core` — the 16-byte opcode engine

### 1.1 The `Opcode` struct

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/opcode.rs:23-38`:

```rust
#[repr(C, packed)]
pub struct Opcode {
    pub category: u8,   // opcode.rs:27
    pub command: u8,    // opcode.rs:29
    pub flags: u16,     // opcode.rs:31
    pub a: u32,         // opcode.rs:33
    pub b: u32,         // opcode.rs:35
    pub c: u32,         // opcode.rs:37
}
```

- `OPCODE_SIZE = 16` (`opcode.rs:15`); `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16` proven at `opcode.rs:156-158`; a 64-byte cache line holds exactly 4.
- All multi-byte fields little-endian on the wire (`opcode.rs:9`). Because the struct is `packed`, reads go through unaligned accessors: `category()`/`command()`/`flags()`/`a()`/`b()`/`c()` (`opcode.rs:59-95`), plus `a_f32()`/`b_f32()`/`c_f32()` bit-preserving f32 views (`opcode.rs:99-113`).

### 1.6 The Guest/Host/Frame surface — what a "frame" is

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/lib.rs`:

- **`init_memory(mem, layout)`** (`lib.rs:78-80`) zeroes the header block once at startup.
- **`Guest`** (producer, `lib.rs:161-397`): owns `header`, `slots`, `event_slots`, `arena`, `event_arena`. API: `begin_frame()` captures `writeCursor` (`lib.rs:198-200`); `pending()` = opcodes since `begin_frame` (`lib.rs:203-207`); `end_frame()` increments `frameCount` (`lib.rs:210-213`); `frame_count()` (`lib.rs:216-218`). Tree builders: `create_node`/`delete_node`/`insert_child`/`remove_child`/`move_child` (`lib.rs:222-245`); `push_opcode` raw escape hatch (`lib.rs:252-254`); `set_property(node_id, prop, value_type, value)` (`lib.rs:258-274`); `set_text(node_id, &str)` arena-allocates and returns the arena ref (`lib.rs:277-281`); `set_date` (`lib.rs:285-295`); `set_design_token` / `set_design_token_string` (`lib.rs:301-344`); `alloc`/`alloc_str` (`lib.rs:347-354`); `reset()` (`lib.rs:358-360`). Event ingress: `drain_events() -> Vec<Event>` (`lib.rs:368-374`), `drain_event_opcodes() -> Vec<Opcode>` (`lib.rs:379-382`), `push_event_opcode(op)` (`lib.rs:394-396`).
- **`Frame<'a>`** (`lib.rs:409-463`): the **transport seam** — a slice of contiguous 16-byte opcodes plus an arena region. Both shared-memory `Host` and network batch decoders produce `Frame` views, so a `RenderTree::apply_frame(frame)` works identically regardless of origin (comment at `lib.rs:403-408`; test proving the interchangeability at `pathland-core-transport/src/batch.rs:433-484`). API: `opcodes()` iterator (`lib.rs:432-438`), `len()`/`is_empty()` (`lib.rs:441-447`), `arena_get(offset)` / `arena_str(offset)` / `arena()` (`lib.rs:450-462`), and the public constructor `Frame::from_parts(slots, arena, start, end)` (`lib.rs:422-429`) used by transport backends. `FrameIter` decodes 16 bytes at a time (`lib.rs:466-483`).
- **`Host`** (consumer, `lib.rs:491-616`): created over the same memory + layout. `frames()` (`lib.rs:532-581`) consumes all opcodes produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor` and updating the `consumed` watermark; returns **at most one coalesced `Frame`** (multiple produced frames merge — `frameCount` merely signals "new data", `lib.rs:487-490`). Guards against a wrapped ring by returning empty (`lib.rs:541-546`). On seeing a `META::RESET` inside the drained slots it resets the host-owned event-arena cursor (`lib.rs:569-578`). `send_event(&Event)` (`lib.rs:592-615`) writes a raw input into the host → guest **event ring**; `TextChanged` text and `Navigate` URLs are bump-allocated into the **event arena** and referenced by their absolute offset in `B`.
- **`SharedHeader`** (`lib.rs:88-141`): immutable header accessors (`frame_count`, `read_cursor`, `write_cursor`, `slot_count`, `ring_offset`, `ring_bytes`, `arena_offset`, `arena_cursor`) for foreign drivers that read the ring **in place** from a raw pointer — exactly what a zero-copy host needs.

The doc example for a host consumer is at `lib.rs:26-43`.

### 1.7 Ring buffer layout

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/ring.rs` + `memory.rs`:

- The ring is a power-of-two slot array of 16-byte slots (`ring.rs:1-5`). Producer writes at `writeCursor`, host reads at `readCursor` — both live in the header block.
- `push` (`ring.rs:24-35`): fails `RingError::Full` when `next == readCursor` (capacity is `slot_count - 1`; proven at `ring.rs:282-300`). Writes `op.to_bytes()` into the slot and advances `writeCursor`.
- Cursor wrapping uses a mask (`slot_count - 1`), `ring.rs:38-41`; the masked cursor may be in the header (values beyond capacity mask correctly, tested `ring.rs:303-309`).
- Host → guest **event ring** is a second ring with the same slot layout: `push_event` at `eventWriteCursor` (`ring.rs:216-232`), `read_events` drains from `eventReadCursor` and only handles contiguous unwrapped runs (`ring.rs:237-260`, wrapped-guard test `ring.rs:358-382`).

### 1.8 Arena layout

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/arena.rs`:

- Bump arena, entries self-describing: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` (`arena.rs:1-5`). Opcodes reference entries by their byte **offset** (`arenaRef`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes.
- `alloc` (`arena.rs:22-24`) uses the guest-owned cursor `OFF_ARENA_CURSOR`; `alloc_event` (`arena.rs:31-37`) uses the host-owned `OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR` (host writes event string payloads the guest resolves over the shared ring).
- `alloc_at` (`arena.rs:41-57`): writes length prefix + bytes, advances cursor, returns the offset. `get`/`get_str` (`arena.rs:71-88`) read entries with bounds checking (`ArenaError::OutOfSpace` / `InvalidOffset`).

## 2. `pathland-engine` — retained tree + diff emitter + signals

Crate root: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/` — `no_std` + `alloc`, depends on `pathland_core` (`lib.rs:8-9`).

### 2.1 Retained tree: `Node` / `Component`

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/node.rs`:

- **`Node`** (`node.rs:20-41`): `id: u32`, `component: Component`, `children: Vec<Node>`, `properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>` (→ `SET_PROPERTY`), `token_properties: BTreeMap<u16, String>` (→ `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY`, overriding literal entries for the same id), `text_binding: Option<SignalId>`, `property_bindings: BTreeMap<u16, SignalId>`, `gestures: Vec<Gesture>` (app-side callbacks, **never** emitted as protocol, `node.rs:38-40`).
- **`Gesture`** (`node.rs:79-83`): only `Tap(Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>)`; `PartialEq` by `Rc::ptr_eq` (`node.rs:85-91`).
- **`Component`** (`node.rs:103-159`): `VStack, HStack, ZStack, Text{text}, Button{label}, Spacer, Image, Color, Shape, Divider, ProgressView, Gauge, Grid, ScrollView, LazyVGrid, LazyHGrid, LazyVStack, LazyHStack, Toggle, Slider, TextField, TextEditor, Stepper, DatePicker, Picker, Menu, ColorPicker`.
- **`component_type_id(&Component) -> u16`** (`node.rs:196-226`) maps each to its protocol id (e.g. `VStack → component_type::VSTACK (0x10)`).
- **`assign_ids(root, next)`** (`node.rs:232-238`) assigns stable sequential ids pre-order (root first) — call after building, before `Engine::emit`.
- **`collect_tap_handlers(root, out)`** (`node.rs:245-255`) walks the tree and produces `BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut()>>>` keyed by node id — the Rust analogue of the Java `tapActions` registry.

### 2.2 The diff emitter (`Engine`)

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/engine.rs`:

- **`Engine`** (`engine.rs:59-66`): holds `snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>` (nodeId → last-emitted state, preallocated slab) + `gen: u64` + `store: SignalStore`.
- **`SnapshotNode`** (`engine.rs:32-45`): `component_type`, `parent`, `index`, `text`, `properties`, `token_refs` (property → (path, arena offset), with the offset **reused** so unchanged token refs never re-allocate into the bump arena), `gen` stamp (detects deletions).
- **`emit(root, &mut Guest) -> Result<EmitResult, RingError>`** (`engine.rs:84-106`): bumps `gen`, clears the signal dependency index, reconciles recursively, then deletes any snapshot node whose `gen` is stale (`engine.rs:96-104`). **Unchanged tree → zero opcodes**; steady state performs zero heap allocations.
- **`reconcile_node`** (`engine.rs:291-492`): resolves `text_binding` (signal `Str` wins over `Component::Text`/`Button` label, `engine.rs:302-325`) and merges `property_bindings` over `properties` (`engine.rs:308-318`). On mount (`prev == None`) emits `CREATE_NODE` + `INSERT_CHILD` + all literal `SET_PROPERTY`s + token refs + `SET_TEXT` (`engine.rs:353-384`). On delta: re-parent via `REMOVE_CHILD`/`INSERT_CHILD`, re-order via `MOVE_CHILD`, component change via re-`CREATE_NODE`, then text/property/token diffs (`engine.rs:385-441`). Records signal deps (`Dep::Text{node}` / `Dep::Property{node, prop}`) at `engine.rs:481-486`.
- **`set_signal(id, value, &mut Guest) -> Result<usize, RingError>`** (`engine.rs:204-260`): if the value actually changed, walks only the recorded deps and emits `SET_TEXT` (for text bindings, `engine.rs:217-233`) or `SET_PROPERTY` (for property bindings, using `value_type_for(prop)`, `engine.rs:234-256`) — **no full tree walk**. Returns the opcode count.
- `EmitResult { opcodes: usize }` (`engine.rs:48-52`).
- `set_design_token` / `apply_theme` / `apply_adaptive_theme` (`engine.rs:117-162`) emit global `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides once at mount (the dark theme gets `dark.` prefix, `engine.rs:153-160`).
- `create_signal` / `get_signal` (`engine.rs:191-198`).

### 2.3 Signals

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/signal.rs`:

- **`SignalValue`** (`signal.rs:20-31`): `F32(f32)`, `U32(u32)`, `Bool(bool)`, `Enum(u8)`, `Str(String)`.
- Packing: `to_property_u32()` (`signal.rs:36-44`) — `F32`→bits, `U32`→raw, `Bool`→`1.0f32`/`0.0f32` bits, `Enum`→`(e as f32).bits`; `Str`→`None` (text-only). `to_text()` (`signal.rs:47-52`).
- **`SignalId(pub u32)`** (`signal.rs:58`) — an FFI-safe index handle.
- **`Dep`** (`signal.rs:62-67`): `Text{node}` | `Property{node, prop}`.
- **`SignalStore`** (`signal.rs:81-144`): `create` (index-based id), `set` (equality-gated, returns changed), `get`, `deps`, `clear_deps`, `add_dep` (deduped). The engine rebuilds the index during each full emit and reuses it for `set_signal`.

### 2.4 `RenderResult` — important correction

**`RenderResult` does NOT exist in the Rust `pathland-engine` crate.** It is a **Java-side record** in `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/emit/RenderResult.java:29-37`:

```java
public record RenderResult(
        int rootId,
        Map<Integer, Runnable> tapActions,
        Map<Integer, Consumer<String>> textInputs,
        Map<Integer, Consumer<Float>> valueInputs,
        Map<Integer, DateInput> dateInputs,
        Map<Integer, MediaInput> mediaInputs,
        Map<Integer, Runnable> navigateActions,
        Consumer<Event> navigateHandler) {}
```

It is returned by `Emitter.mount(root, env)` (`Emitter.java:79,108`). The maps are **live unmodifiable views** (`RenderResult.java:12-15`) so a structural reconcile (a `Conditional.when` branch swap, navigation destination change) keeps them current. The host routes raw events through them — the Java `InputDispatcher` (`InputDispatcher.java:18-109`) maps `PointerUp→tapActions`/`navigateActions`, `TextChanged→textInputs`, `ValueChanged→valueInputs`, `DateChanged→dateInputs`, `Media*→mediaInputs`, `Navigate(url)→activePath`, `Navigate(back)→navigateHandler`.

The **Rust** equivalents of those registries are:
- `Node::gestures` + `collect_tap_handlers` (`pathland-engine/src/node.rs:245-255`) for taps;
- `pathland-view`'s `TapRecognizer` (`lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/src/recognizer.rs:23`) which consumes pointer events;
- On the **host/renderer side**, the reference Rust renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`) keeps its own retained map and routes via an `event_sink: Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut(Event)>>` (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:84`), writing events into the pump (`lib.rs:2106-2116`).

## 3. `pathland-core-transport` — ring, network batches, batching

Crate root: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/` (std). Two peer backends: shared-memory ring (zero-copy, local) and network batch (SSR → browser) (`lib.rs:4-10`).

### 3.1 `RingTransport`

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/ring.rs`:

- **`RingTransport`** (`ring.rs:19-24`) owns the linear-memory `Vec<u8>` + `MemoryLayout` — this is the **owner of the shared buffer** (SPSC: producer = guest/engine, consumer = host/renderer; doc at `ring.rs:1-7`).
- `new()` (`ring.rs:28-33`) default layout + zeroed header; `with_buffer(mem, layout)` (`ring.rs:36-38`).
- `producer()` (`ring.rs:49-51`) grants a short-lived `Guest` over the same buffer — **drop the `Guest` before calling `next_frame`** (borrows must not overlap). `buffer()` (`ring.rs:54-56`) peeks the raw bytes.
- **`FrameSource for RingTransport`** (`ring.rs:65-77`): `next_frame()` builds a `Host`, drains `host.frames()`, and wraps the coalesced frame in `OpcodeBatch::new(frame, GUEST_TO_HOST)`.
- **`DriverTransport for RingTransport`** (`ring.rs:79-88`): `send_input(&Event)` → `Host::send_event` into the event ring.
- `drain_events()` (`ring.rs:93-97`) → guest side reads typed events back.
- Zero-copy is proven at `ring.rs:178-254` (1000-opcode read allocates O(1); arena string pointer lies inside the shared buffer).

### 3.2 Network batch encode/decode (PLPL format)

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/batch.rs`:

- **Wire format** (`batch.rs:27-33`, `lib.rs:28-37`):
  ```
  magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16=1) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32) | opcodeCount (u32)
  | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | stringsLen (u32) | string bytes (length-prefixed entries [u32 len][bytes])
  ```
  `BATCH_HEADER = 16` (`batch.rs:9`), `BATCH_MAGIC = 0x504C_504C`, `BATCH_VERSION = 1` (`lib.rs:76-78`).
- `encode_batch(frame_count, flags, opcodes, arena_delta)` (`batch.rs:88-106`); `parse` (`batch.rs:117-163`) validates magic/version/counts.
- **Two codecs** (`lib.rs:13-26`):
  - **Arena-delta batches**: `BatchEncoder` (`batch.rs:172-210`) tracks `last_arena_len` and ships only appended arena bytes; `META::RESET` restarts tracking. `BatchDecoder` (`batch.rs:218-260`) maintains a **mirrored arena**, appends each delta, clears on RESET, and exposes the result as a `Frame` (`batch.rs:248`). `SET_TEXT` offsets are absolute arena offsets. This is the ring-compatible codec (future WASM/embedded).
  - **Self-contained frames**: `encode_frame`/`decode_frame` (`batch.rs:372-402`) — each batch carries its own string section and `SET_TEXT` uses **relative** offsets; the consumer needs no prior state. This is the WebSocket streaming codec (`lib.rs:18-19`).
- **Events on the wire**: `encode_events(frame_count, &[Event])` (`batch.rs:269-304`) uses the `HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag, pushing `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE(URL)` strings into the batch's string section; `decode_events(bytes)` (`batch.rs:310-341`) decodes back to `(frame_count, Vec<Event>)`.
- `encode_resync()` (`batch.rs:379-386`) — a `META::RESYNC` host→guest request batch.
- `frame_from_slices` (`batch.rs:350-359`) — in-process `Frame` view with no serialization.
- Direction flags: `GUEST_TO_HOST=0x0000`, `HOST_TO_GUEST=0x0001` (`lib.rs:81-85`).

### 3.3 Batching policy

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/batching.rs`:

- `BatchPolicy { max_interval: Duration, max_batch_bytes: usize }` (`batching.rs:23-28`); defaults `DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL = 4 ms`, `DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES = 1400` (`batching.rs:17-19`).
- **`Batcher`** (`batching.rs:57-160`): `push_frame(frame_count, opcodes, arena_used)` accumulates opcodes + the arena delta since the last flush (`batching.rs:109-125`, tracking `last_arena_len`, resetting pending arena if it shrank). `flush(force)` (`batching.rs:139-159`) serializes when **either** the time interval since the first buffered opcode elapsed **or** the byte size reached the threshold — first trigger wins.

### 3.4 How a renderer reads frames and writes events

The abstraction is in `traits.rs`:

- **`OpcodeBatch<'a>`** (`traits.rs:21-42`): wraps a `Frame` + a direction bitmask.
- **`FrameSource`** (`traits.rs:80-86`): `fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch>, TransportError>` — the read side.
- **`InputSink`** (`traits.rs:70-73`): `fn dispatch(&mut self, &Event)`.
- **`DriverTransport`** (`traits.rs:89-92`): `FrameSource + fn send_input(&mut self, &Event)` — the renderer's write side.
- `TransportError` (`traits.rs:46-53`): `Backpressure` / `Closed` / `Protocol(ProtocolError)`; `ProtocolError` (`traits.rs:57-64`): `BadVersion` / `Malformed` / `BadInput`.

A Ratatui renderer would implement `FrameSource` (+ `DriverTransport`) over a `RingTransport`, or consume the transport-agnostic `Frame` directly via the GTK renderer's pattern: `renderer.apply_frame(batch.frame())` (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:2215-2218`) and `pump.send_input(&ev)` (`lib.rs:2106-2116`).

## 4. `pathland-view-native` — NativeHost + the flat C ABI

Crate root: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view-native/src/` — the **cross-language, zero-copy** desktop path (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) linking the `cdylib` (`lib.rs:1-13`).

### 4.1 `NativeHost`

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-view-native/src/lib.rs`:

- **`FlatNode`** (`lib.rs:28-38`): `id`, `view_component: pathland_view::Component`, `properties: BTreeMap<u16,u32>`, `text_binding: Option<SignalId>`, `property_bindings: BTreeMap<u16, SignalId>`, `parent: Option<u32>`, `children: Vec<u32>` — a flat id-keyed retained tree.
- **`NativeHost`** (`lib.rs:42-46`): `nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>` + `engine: Engine` + `ring: RingTransport`. **It owns all three**: the flat tree, the diff engine, and the shared ring.
- `new()` (`lib.rs:57-63`) / `with_buffer(mem, layout)` (`lib.rs:66-72`).
- Operations: `create_node` (resets a node's properties/bindings, `lib.rs:75-89`), `insert_child`/`remove_child` (index handling with `u32::MAX` append, `lib.rs:92-116`), `set_text` (only for `Text`/`Button` components, `lib.rs:119-127`), `set_property`/`set_property_f32` (`lib.rs:131-140`), `bind_text`/`bind_property` (`lib.rs:144-161`), `create_signal`/`get_signal` (`lib.rs:164-171`).
- **`set_signal`** (`lib.rs:177-183`): wraps `engine.set_signal` in a `begin_frame`/`end_frame` pair on the ring's producer — a **partial emit**.
- **`emit`** (`lib.rs:188-199`): materializes the flat tree into a `pathland_engine::Node` root (`materialize`, `lib.rs:226-239`), then `engine.emit(&root, &mut guest)` inside a frame.
- **`ring_buffer()`** (`lib.rs:202-204`) exposes the linear memory for FFI/embedding; `take_ring()` (`lib.rs:207-209`); `layout()` (`lib.rs:212-214`); `root_id()` (`lib.rs:221-223`).
- Trait impls: **`FrameSource`** (`lib.rs:250-254`, delegates to `ring.next_frame()` — a renderer drains guest→host frames here) and **`DriverTransport`** (`lib.rs:257-261`, delegates `send_input` — the renderer writes host→guest events here). Guest-side `drain_events()` (`lib.rs:266-268`).
- `component_from_id` (raw u32 → `Component`, `lib.rs:272-304`), `component_id` (reverse, `lib.rs:307-309`), and `property_value_type` (derives `(prop, value_type)` for the C ABI, `lib.rs:313-360`).

### 4.3 How a host consumes frames zero-copy and drains events

The pattern (documented in the header comment, `capi.rs:8-17`):
1. `h = pathland_native_create()`.
2. Build the tree via `pathland_native_create_node`/`set_text`/`set_property`/`insert_child`; optionally bind signals.
3. `pathland_native_emit(h)` — the engine diffs into the shared ring.
4. Read `pathland_native_ring_ptr(h)` + `ring_len`, parse the header at offset 0: `frameCount@0x26` signals new data, `readCursor@0x1E`/`writeCursor@0x22` delimit the frame, `ringOffset@0x06`/`arenaOffset@0x12` locate regions — then read the 16-byte opcodes **in place**.
5. To send raw inputs back, the renderer uses `DriverTransport::send_input`/`Host::send_event` (or, from C, pushes `EVENT` opcodes); the host is woken and calls `pathland_native_drain_events` to copy the pending event opcodes out.

There is also the **minimal ring C ABI** `libpathland_core` (`pathland-core-capi/src/lib.rs`), used by the Java DSL via JNA when the host owns the retained tree + diff itself: `pathland_core_create` (`capi:58`), `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (`capi:81`), `pathland_core_arena_alloc` (`capi:93`), `pathland_core_begin_frame`/`end_frame`/`frame_count` (`capi:109-126`), `pathland_core_ring_ptr`/`ring_len`/`ring_mut` (`capi:131-152`), `pathland_core_drain_events` (`capi:162-179`), `pathland_core_send_event` (`capi:184-190`).

## 5. How events flow (the bidirectional event ring)

### The ring and arena

- **Two rings in one shared memory**: the guest → host ring (frames) at `ringOffset` and the host → guest **event ring** at `eventRingOffset`, same 16-byte slot layout (`memory.rs:44-52`, `lib.rs:165`). Each has its own cursors in the header: guest writes frames at `writeCursor` (`0x22`), host reads at `readCursor` (`0x1E`); host writes events at `eventWriteCursor` (`0x3A`), guest reads at `eventReadCursor` (`0x36`).
- **Two arenas**: the guest-owned bump arena (tree strings, `arenaCursor@0x1A`) and the **host-owned event arena** (`eventArenaCursor@0x48`) for host → guest event strings (`memory.rs:57-58`; `arena.rs:31-37`).
- Events are **always 16-byte `EVENT`-category opcodes** — never a side-channel callback.

### Who writes, who drains, the wake

1. **Renderer writes** raw inputs into the event ring. The GTK renderer collects native inputs (pointer gesture, motion, scroll controllers; control signals; window-level Escape/BackSpace for back-navigation) into its `event_sink` (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:84, 712-729, 2121`), which calls the shared `emit` closure (`lib.rs:2102-2116`):
   ```
   let _ = p.send_input(&ev);   // writes the EVENT opcode into the pump
   drop(p);
   wake.borrow_mut()(pump.clone());   // wakes the host
   ```
   `send_input` is `DriverTransport::send_input` → `Host::send_event` (`pathland-core/src/lib.rs:592-615`), which bump-allocates `TextChanged`/`Navigate` strings into the **event arena** and writes the opcode at `eventWriteCursor` via `push_event` (`ring.rs:216-232`). Control signals that fire re-entrantly during a frame apply are deferred to a pending queue and flushed before the next frame (`lib.rs:2101-2115`, `2187-2205`).

2. **The renderer never drains events** — documented at `pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:49-56` ("The renderer **never drains events** — it only writes them as `EVENT` opcodes. The host (application) drains the event ring itself").

3. **Wake mechanism**: the `on_event` callback — a plain `extern "C" fn()` with **no payload** (`pathland-render-gtk/src/capi.rs:25`). After writing an event the renderer invokes it (`lib.rs:2110`, `2204`); the host then drains. On the C ABI surface: `pathland_native_drain_events(host, out, max)` copies the raw opcodes (`capi.rs:191-207`), or `pathland_core_drain_events` over a `libpathland_core` ring (`pathland-core-capi/src/lib.rs:162-179`). The Rust app path is `Guest::drain_events()` (`pathland-core/src/lib.rs:368-374`), which decodes each opcode with the event arena via `decode_event` (`events.rs:444-462`).

4. **Host drains**: the application polls `drain_events` and routes the typed `Event`s into its state — on the Java side through `InputDispatcher` (`InputDispatcher.java:48-109`); on the Rust side through the app's tap handlers / signal writes. Events are only gated by `EVENT_LISTENERS` (which raw inputs a node wants) and `BINDING_ID` (value/text events; `pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:467-471`).

5. **The idle pump** (`lib.rs:2161-2169`) applies pending frames to the renderer via `pump_once` (`lib.rs:2209-2219`) — events flow the other way.

## Practical notes for a Ratatui renderer

- **Host surface you need**: `pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout, Frame, Event, Opcode, SharedHeader}` + `pathland_core_transport::{RingTransport, FrameSource, DriverTransport, OpcodeBatch}`. The reference consumer loop is `pump_once` in the GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:2209-2219`): `next_frame() → apply_frame(batch.frame())`.
- **`RenderTree::apply_frame`** (`pathland-render-gtk/src/host.rs:173-270`) is the canonical decoder — it turns TREE/PARAMETER opcodes into a retained `HostNode` map (`host.rs:18-40`) with `properties`, resolved `strings`, and `token_refs`. A Ratatui renderer would reuse this exact struct (it has no GTK dependency) and map nodes to Ratatui widgets.
- **Events to emit for TUI**: `PointerDown/Up` (mouse), `KeyDown/Up` (keyboard), `Scroll`/`Wheel`, `FocusChanged`/`Submit` for text inputs — all gated per-node by the `EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask (`constants.rs:152-176`). `TextChanged`/`Navigate(URL)` strings must go through the event arena / string section (see `Host::send_event`, `pathland-core/src/lib.rs:592-615`).
- **`META::ENVIRONMENT`** (`VIEWPORT_WIDTH`/`VIEWPORT_HEIGHT`, `constants.rs:121-128`) is how a host reports terminal size to the guest.
- **Statelessness rule**: the renderer retains only its rendered-output tree + computed layout (its cache); all application state lives in the guest (`AGENTS.md` Principle 1).
- **Value-type decode**: use `value_type_for(prop)` (`constants.rs:546-582`) and the `B` high byte `(op.b() >> 16) as u8` (as `host.rs:222` does) to interpret `SET_PROPERTY` payloads.
